board_events.text: Aldehyde: the carbonyl carbon carries at least one H (R–CHO).
Ketone: the carbonyl carbon is flanked by two carbons (R–CO–R$'$).
The whole chapter turns on one question: is there an H on the carbonyl carbon?
Sharing the formula $C_nH_{2n}O$ makes aldehydes and ketones functional isomers.
Nature's carbonyls: vanillin and cinnamaldehyde are aldehydes; camphor and carvone are ketones.

segments.text: <curious> Let me introduce the single most important character in this entire chapter.
The carbonyl group is just a carbon double-bonded to an oxygen, and we write it C double bond O.
Look at the two cases here. The carbon in the middle is the carbonyl carbon, and everything depends on what sits next to it.
If that carbon carries at least one hydrogen, the molecule is an aldehyde, written R C H O.
If instead it is flanked by two carbon groups, the molecule is a ketone, written R C O R prime.
So the whole chapter turns on one tiny question: is there a hydrogen sitting on the carbonyl carbon, or not?
Notice that both families share the same general formula, C n H two n O, for the saturated aliphatic case.
Because they share that formula, aldehydes and ketones are functional isomers of one another.
<chuckle> And here is a lovely window into it: vanillin and cinnamaldehyde are aldehydes, while camphor and carvone are ketones. The same carbonyl that makes them reactive also makes them smell.
<curious> चलिए इस पूरे chapter के सबसे important character से मिलते हैं।
Carbonyl group का मतलब है एक carbon जो oxygen से double bond बनाता है, जिसे हम लिखते हैं C double bond O।
यहाँ दोनों cases देखिए। बीच वाला carbon ही carbonyl carbon है, और सब कुछ इसके आस-पास पर depend करता है।
अगर उस carbon पर कम से कम एक hydrogen है, तो molecule एक aldehyde है, जिसे R C H O लिखते हैं।
लेकिन अगर उसके दोनों तरफ़ carbon groups हैं, तो यह एक ketone है, जिसे R C O R prime लिखते हैं।
तो पूरा chapter एक छोटे से सवाल पर टिका है: carbonyl carbon पर hydrogen है या नहीं?
ध्यान दीजिए, दोनों families का general formula एक ही है, C n H two n O, saturated aliphatic case के लिए।
इसी वजह से aldehydes और ketones एक दूसरे के functional isomers होते हैं।
<chuckle> और एक प्यारी बात: vanillin और cinnamaldehyde aldehydes हैं, जबकि camphor और carvone ketones हैं। जो carbonyl इन्हें reactive बनाता है, वही इन्हें smell भी देता है।

board_events.text: Steric: a ketone crowds the carbonyl carbon with two groups; an aldehyde leaves one side open.
Electronic: oxygen pulls the shared electrons, so the carbon is $\delta+$ (electrophilic).
Each alkyl group gently pushes electron density onto the carbon, softening that $\delta+$.
The rule is a default, not a law: $CCl_3CHO$ beats acetaldehyde; benzaldehyde is de-activated by the ring.

segments.text: Here is a rule you will use constantly: aldehydes are generally more reactive than ketones toward nucleophilic addition.
What makes it reliable is that two completely independent reasons both push in the same direction.
Picture the carbonyl carbon as a doorway that incoming reagents try to enter.
The steric reason: in a ketone, two alkyl groups block the doorway; in an aldehyde one side is just a small hydrogen, so a nucleophile pushes in far more easily.
The electronic reason: oxygen is greedier for electrons, so the carbonyl carbon carries a partial positive charge and behaves as an electrophilic centre.
Now, each attached alkyl group gently pushes electron density toward that carbon and softens the delta plus. A ketone has two such pushers, an aldehyde only one.
So the reactivity order to memorise is methanal, greater than ethanal, greater than propanone.

<whisper> But treat it as a strong default, not a law. Trichloroacetaldehyde beats ordinary acetaldehyde because the chlorines pull electrons away, and benzaldehyde is de-activated because the ring donates electrons in.
एक rule जो आप बार-बार use करेंगे: aldehydes generally ketones से ज़्यादा reactive होते हैं nucleophilic addition के लिए।
इसे reliable इसलिए माना जाता है क्योंकि दो बिल्कुल अलग reasons एक ही direction में point करते हैं।
Carbonyl carbon को एक दरवाज़े की तरह सोचिए जिसमें incoming reagents घुसने की कोशिश करते हैं।
Steric reason: ketone में दो alkyl groups दरवाज़ा block करते हैं, जबकि aldehyde में एक तरफ़ सिर्फ़ छोटा hydrogen है, तो nucleophile आसानी से घुस जाता है।
Electronic reason: oxygen electrons का ज़्यादा भूखा है, इसलिए carbonyl carbon पर partial positive charge आता है और वह electrophilic centre बन जाता है।
अब, हर attached alkyl group उस carbon पर थोड़ी electron density push करता है और delta plus को soft कर देता है। Ketone में दो pushers हैं, aldehyde में सिर्फ़ एक।
तो याद रखने वाला reactivity order है methanal, greater than ethanal, greater than propanone।

<whisper> लेकिन इसे एक strong default मानिए, law नहीं। Trichloroacetaldehyde ordinary acetaldehyde से आगे है क्योंकि chlorines electrons खींच लेते हैं, और benzaldehyde de-activated है क्योंकि ring electrons donate करता है।

board_events.text: The numbers and notation to memorise
Suffixes: aldehyde $\to$ -al; ketone $\to$ -one; ring-CHO $\to$ -carbaldehyde.
Aldehyde beats ketone; aliphatic beats aromatic — but always audit the substituents.

segments.text: Let me give you the toolkit of numbers and notation for this sub-topic; keep these on instant recall.
The carbonyl carbon is s p two hybridised, so its three bonds spread to roughly one hundred twenty degrees in one plane.
The C double bond O is short and tight: about one hundred twenty three picometres, shorter than a C double bond C at about one hundred thirty four.
It is also strong, about seven hundred forty five kilojoules per mole, and strongly polar, with a dipole moment of about two point three to two point eight debye.
For naming: drop the alkane's final e and add -al for an aldehyde or -one for a ketone; a C H O on a ring uses -carbaldehyde.
For the suffix priority, the higher group claims the principal suffix: acid, then ester, acid chloride, amide, nitrile, aldehyde, ketone, alcohol, and finally amine.
The core reactivity number: methanal, greater than ethanal, greater than propanone.
And the aromatic series: phenylacetaldehyde, greater than benzaldehyde, greater than acetophenone, greater than benzophenone.
<whisper> The headline is aldehyde beats ketone and aliphatic beats aromatic, but always audit what the substituents are doing to that carbonyl carbon's positive charge.
चलिए इस sub-topic के numbers और notation का toolkit दे देता हूँ; इन्हें instant recall पर रखिए।
Carbonyl carbon s p two hybridised है, इसलिए इसके तीन bonds एक plane में लगभग एक सौ बीस degrees पर फैलते हैं।
C double bond O छोटा और tight है: लगभग एक सौ तेईस picometres, जो C double bond C के एक सौ चौंतीस से छोटा है।
यह strong भी है, लगभग सात सौ पैंतालीस kilojoules per mole, और काफ़ी polar, dipole moment करीब दो दशमलव तीन से दो दशमलव आठ debye।
Naming के लिए: alkane का आख़िरी e हटाइए और aldehyde के लिए -al या ketone के लिए -one लगाइए; ring पर C H O के लिए -carbaldehyde use होता है।
Suffix priority में, ऊपर वाला group principal suffix लेता है: acid, फिर ester, acid chloride, amide, nitrile, aldehyde, ketone, alcohol, और आख़िर में amine।
Core reactivity number: methanal, greater than ethanal, greater than propanone।
और aromatic series: phenylacetaldehyde, greater than benzaldehyde, greater than acetophenone, greater than benzophenone।
<whisper> Headline है aldehyde beats ketone और aliphatic beats aromatic, लेकिन हमेशा check कीजिए कि substituents उस carbonyl carbon के positive charge के साथ क्या कर रहे हैं।

board_events.text: Building the C=O bond, step by step
The carbonyl carbon makes three $\sigma$ bonds and has no lone pairs, so it is $sp^2$ hybridised.
Three $sp^2$ orbitals point to a triangle's corners, fixing $\approx 120^\circ$ and a flat, planar centre.
A head-on overlap builds the C–O $\sigma$ bond; the leftover $p$ orbitals overlap sideways for the $\pi$ bond.
The $\pi$ cloud sits above and below the plane — this is where nucleophiles attack.
Oxygen pulls the $\pi$ and $\sigma$ electrons across, giving $C^{\delta+}=O^{\delta-}$.

board_events.text: The dipolar contributor explains the large dipole and confirms the carbon is electrophilic.

segments.text: Let us actually build the carbonyl's electronic structure, because the reasoning powers every reaction later.
The carbonyl carbon forms three sigma bonds and carries no lone pairs, so it needs three equivalent in-plane orbitals: it is s p two hybridised.
Those three s p two orbitals point to the corners of a triangle, which fixes the bond angles near one hundred twenty degrees and forces the centre to be flat and planar.
One s p two orbital overlaps head-on to make the carbon-oxygen sigma bond; the leftover unhybridised p orbitals overlap sideways to make the pi bond.
That pi electron cloud sits above and below the molecular plane, and this is exactly where an incoming nucleophile will attack.
Because oxygen is more electronegative, it drags the pi and sigma electrons toward itself, giving a carbon that is delta plus and an oxygen that is delta minus.
Look at the resonance picture. We draw the carbonyl as a hybrid of a neutral form and a charge-separated, dipolar form.
In symbols, C double bond O is in resonance with C plus, single bond, O minus.
That dipolar contributor is what explains the unusually large dipole moment and confirms the carbon's electrophilic character.
चलिए carbonyl का electronic structure सच में बनाते हैं, क्योंकि यही reasoning आगे हर reaction को चलाती है।
Carbonyl carbon तीन sigma bonds बनाता है और कोई lone pair नहीं रखता, इसलिए इसे तीन equivalent in-plane orbitals चाहिए: यह s p two hybridised है।
ये तीन s p two orbitals एक triangle के corners की तरफ़ point करते हैं, जो bond angles को एक सौ बीस degrees के पास fix करता है और centre को flat, planar बना देता है।
एक s p two orbital head-on overlap करके carbon-oxygen sigma bond बनाता है; बचे हुए unhybridised p orbitals sideways overlap करके pi bond बनाते हैं।
वह pi electron cloud molecular plane के ऊपर और नीचे बैठता है, और यही वह जगह है जहाँ incoming nucleophile attack करेगा।
क्योंकि oxygen ज़्यादा electronegative है, वह pi और sigma electrons को अपनी तरफ़ खींचता है, जिससे carbon delta plus और oxygen delta minus हो जाता है।
Resonance picture देखिए। हम carbonyl को एक neutral form और एक charge-separated, dipolar form के hybrid के रूप में draw करते हैं।
Symbols में, C double bond O resonance में है C plus, single bond, O minus के साथ।
यही dipolar contributor उस unusually बड़े dipole moment को समझाता है और carbon के electrophilic character को confirm करता है।

board_events.text: Aldehyde -CHO is terminal, so it is C-1 by definition — never write a locant on it.
For a ketone, number from the nearer end so the C=O gets the lowest locant.
Rings: -CHO $\to$ -carbaldehyde; ring C=O $\to$ cycloalkanone; aryl $\to$ benzaldehyde.
Add substituents alphabetically with locants as prefixes.
Functional-isomer flag: propanal, propanone and prop-2-en-1-ol are all $C_3H_6O$.

segments.text: Naming is a mechanical skill you must reproduce on demand, so let us fix the five moves.
Move one: choose the longest continuous carbon chain that actually contains the carbonyl carbon.
Move two: drop the parent alkane's final e and add -al for an aldehyde or -one for a ketone.
Move three is the numbering, and the diagram shows the trap. Number from the end nearer the carbonyl.
For an aldehyde the C H O carbon is at the end by definition, so it is carbon one automatically. Never put a locant on it.
For a ketone, number from whichever end gives the carbonyl the lowest locant, so you write pentan-two-one, never pentan-four-one.
For rings, a C H O uses -carbaldehyde, a ring carbonyl becomes a cycloalkanone, and the simplest aryl aldehyde is just benzaldehyde.
Finally, add any substituents in alphabetical order with their locants as prefixes.
And a quick isomer flag worth carrying: propanal, propanone and prop-two-en-one-ol all share the formula C three H six O.
Naming एक mechanical skill है जो आपको on demand reproduce करनी है, तो पाँच moves fix कर लेते हैं।
Move एक: सबसे लंबी continuous carbon chain चुनिए जिसमें carbonyl carbon actually में हो।
Move दो: parent alkane का आख़िरी e हटाइए और aldehyde के लिए -al या ketone के लिए -one लगाइए।
Move तीन है numbering, और diagram trap दिखाता है। Carbonyl के नज़दीक वाले end से number कीजिए।
Aldehyde में C H O carbon by definition end पर है, इसलिए वह automatically carbon one है। उस पर कभी locant मत लगाइए।
Ketone के लिए उस end से number कीजिए जो carbonyl को सबसे छोटा locant दे, तो आप लिखेंगे pentan-two-one, कभी pentan-four-one नहीं।
Rings के लिए, C H O -carbaldehyde use करता है, ring carbonyl cycloalkanone बन जाता है, और सबसे simple aryl aldehyde बस benzaldehyde है।
आख़िर में, substituents को alphabetical order में उनके locants के साथ prefix की तरह लगाइए।
और एक isomer flag याद रखिए: propanal, propanone और prop-two-en-one-ol सभी का formula C three H six O है।

board_events.text: Oxidise a 1$^\circ$ alcohol $\to$ aldehyde; a 2$^\circ$ alcohol $\to$ ketone.
A strong oxidant runs the aldehyde on to an acid — use a mild one (PCC) to stop.
Passing alcohol vapour over hot Cu at $\approx 573$ K strips $H_2$: dehydrogenation to the same products.
Reductive ozonolysis cleaves a C=C into two carbonyl fragments.
Alkyne hydration gives a ketone — ethyne is the single exception, giving ethanal.

segments.text: Let us organise preparation as routes that make both families, then routes specific to one. Start with the common routes.
The diagram lays out the four shared routes; keep this map in your head as we walk through them.
First, oxidation of alcohols. A primary alcohol has just the right number of hydrogens to stop at an aldehyde; a secondary alcohol goes to a ketone.
But watch out: a strong oxidant does not stop, it drives the aldehyde onward to a carboxylic acid. So when the aldehyde is the target, use a mild oxidant like P C C.
Second, catalytic dehydrogenation. Pass the alcohol vapour over heated copper at about five hundred seventy three kelvin and it simply loses hydrogen, giving the same aldehyde or ketone cleanly.
Third, reductive ozonolysis cleaves a carbon-carbon double bond and caps each carbon with an oxygen, giving two carbonyl fragments.
In symbols, the alkene splits under ozone then zinc and water into two carbonyl pieces.
<excited> Fourth, hydration of an alkyne gives a ketone, and here is the exam favourite: ethyne is the one exception, giving the aldehyde ethanal instead.
Preparation को ऐसे organise करते हैं: पहले वो routes जो दोनों families बनाते हैं, फिर वो जो सिर्फ़ एक के लिए specific हैं। Common routes से शुरू करते हैं।
Diagram चारों shared routes को लाता है; इस map को दिमाग़ में रखिए जब हम इन्हें cover करें।
पहला, alcohols का oxidation। Primary alcohol में बिल्कुल सही number के hydrogens होते हैं जो aldehyde पर रुक जाते हैं; secondary alcohol ketone तक जाता है।
लेकिन सावधान: strong oxidant रुकता नहीं, वह aldehyde को आगे carboxylic acid तक ले जाता है। तो जब aldehyde target हो, P C C जैसा mild oxidant use कीजिए।
दूसरा, catalytic dehydrogenation। Alcohol vapour को लगभग पाँच सौ तिहत्तर kelvin पर heated copper के ऊपर से गुज़ारिए, वह बस hydrogen खो देता है और वही aldehyde या ketone cleanly देता है।
तीसरा, reductive ozonolysis एक carbon-carbon double bond को cleave करता है और हर carbon पर एक oxygen लगा देता है, दो carbonyl fragments देता है।
Symbols में, alkene ozone फिर zinc और water के साथ टूट कर दो carbonyl pieces में बदल जाता है।
<excited> चौथा, alkyne का hydration एक ketone देता है, और यहाँ exam favourite है: ethyne अकेला exception है, जो इसकी जगह aldehyde ethanal देता है।

board_events.text: Rosenmund: acyl chloride + $H_2$ over $Pd/BaSO_4$, a deliberately poisoned catalyst.
The poison makes the catalyst just active enough to reach the aldehyde and no further.
From nitriles: Stephen ($SnCl_2/HCl$) or DIBAL-H stop at an imine that hydrolyses to the aldehyde.
Aromatic aldehydes: Étard ($CrO_2Cl_2$), side-chain chlorination, Gattermann-Koch ($CO+HCl$).
Ketones: dialkylcadmium + acyl chloride, Grignard + nitrile, Friedel-Crafts acylation.
Cadmium is mild and stops at the ketone; a Grignard would over-shoot to a 3$^\circ$ alcohol.

segments.text: Now the routes specific to one family. Every one of these is engineered to stop where you want it and not over-run.
The diagram splits them: aldehyde-only routes on the left, ketone-only routes on the right.
For aldehydes, the classic is Rosenmund reduction: an acyl chloride with hydrogen over palladium on barium sulphate.
The trick is that the barium sulphate support, often with a little sulphur or quinoline, deliberately poisons the catalyst so it is just active enough to reach the aldehyde and no further.
From nitriles you have two options: the Stephen reaction with tin chloride and H C l, or D I B A L-H; both stop at an imine that hydrolyses to the aldehyde.
For aromatic aldehydes remember three names: the Etard reaction with chromyl chloride, side-chain chlorination then hydrolysis, and Gattermann-Koch using carbon monoxide and H C l.
For ketones, three routes: dialkylcadmium with an acyl chloride, a Grignard reagent with a nitrile, and Friedel-Crafts acylation for aryl ketones.
<whisper> Why cadmium and not Grignard for the acyl chloride? Cadmium is mild and stops cleanly at the ketone, whereas a Grignard would attack again and over-shoot to a tertiary alcohol.
अब वो routes जो एक family के लिए specific हैं। इनमें से हर एक ऐसे engineered है कि वह वहीं रुके जहाँ आप चाहते हैं, आगे न भागे।
Diagram इन्हें अलग करता है: aldehyde-only routes बायीं तरफ़, ketone-only routes दायीं तरफ़।
Aldehydes के लिए classic है Rosenmund reduction: एक acyl chloride, hydrogen के साथ, palladium on barium sulphate पर।
Trick यह है कि barium sulphate support, अक्सर थोड़े sulphur या quinoline के साथ, जान-बूझकर catalyst को poison करता है ताकि वह बस इतना active रहे कि aldehyde तक पहुँचे और आगे नहीं।
Nitriles से दो options हैं: Stephen reaction tin chloride और H C l के साथ, या D I B A L-H; दोनों एक imine पर रुकते हैं जो hydrolyse होकर aldehyde देता है।
Aromatic aldehydes के लिए तीन नाम याद रखिए: Etard reaction chromyl chloride के साथ, side-chain chlorination फिर hydrolysis, और Gattermann-Koch carbon monoxide और H C l के साथ।
Ketones के लिए तीन routes: dialkylcadmium एक acyl chloride के साथ, एक Grignard reagent एक nitrile के साथ, और aryl ketones के लिए Friedel-Crafts acylation।
<whisper> Acyl chloride के लिए cadmium क्यों, Grignard क्यों नहीं? Cadmium mild है और ketone पर cleanly रुक जाता है, जबकि Grignard दोबारा attack करके tertiary alcohol तक over-shoot कर जाता।

board_events.text: It is a ketone: the carbonyl is flanked by two carbons.
Principal chain: the longest chain through the C=O is five carbons $\Rightarrow$ pentane.
Suffix: ketone $\Rightarrow$ pentan-?-one.
Numbering: from the right the carbonyl is C-2; from the left it would be C-4. Choose C-2.
Substituent: a methyl branch sits on C-4.
Common name isobutyl methyl ketone — recognise it, but the IUPAC name earns the mark.

segments.text: Let us name a ketone cleanly, the kind of one-to-two mark question C B S E almost always sets.
Look at the structure and its numbering in the diagram as we go.
First, identify the family: the carbonyl is flanked by two carbon groups, so this is a ketone.
Step one, the principal chain: the longest chain running through the carbonyl is five carbons, so the parent is pentane.
Step two, the suffix: a ketone gives us pentan-something-one.
Step three, the numbering: counting from the right the carbonyl is at carbon two, but from the left it would be carbon four. We choose the lower locant, carbon two.
Step four, the substituent: there is a methyl branch, and it sits on carbon four.
Putting it together, the name is four-methylpentan-two-one.
Its common name is isobutyl methyl ketone. Recognise that, but remember the I U P A C name is what earns the mark.
चलिए एक ketone को cleanly name करते हैं, वही one-to-two mark question जो C B S E लगभग हमेशा पूछता है।
Structure और उसकी numbering diagram में देखते चलिए।
पहले family पहचानिए: carbonyl दोनों तरफ़ carbon groups से घिरा है, तो यह एक ketone है।
Step एक, principal chain: carbonyl से गुज़रती सबसे लंबी chain पाँच carbons की है, तो parent pentane है।
Step दो, suffix: ketone हमें pentan-something-one देता है।
Step तीन, numbering: दायें से गिनने पर carbonyl carbon two पर है, लेकिन बायें से वह carbon four होता। हम छोटा locant, carbon two, चुनते हैं।
Step चार, substituent: एक methyl branch है, और वह carbon four पर बैठा है।
सब जोड़ने पर नाम है four-methylpentan-two-one।
इसका common name isobutyl methyl ketone है। उसे पहचानिए, लेकिन याद रखिए कि I U P A C नाम ही mark दिलाता है।

board_events.text: The trap: writing 'aldehyde before ketone' and stopping — one aldehyde is super-charged.
Shortcut: rank by how positive the carbonyl carbon is.
$CCl_3CHO$: three chlorines pull electrons away, so the carbon is most electron-poor.
Methanal: zero electron-pushing alkyls, so it comes next.
Ethanal has one $+I$ methyl; propanone has two plus steric crowding, so it is least.

segments.text: This is a classic N E E T speed trap on reactivity toward nucleophilic addition, and it is solvable in under ten seconds.
The diagram ranks the four molecules by how electron-poor the carbonyl carbon is; that ranking is the whole answer.
<curious> Here is the trap: students mechanically write aldehyde before ketone and stop, but one of these aldehydes is super-charged.
The mental shortcut is to rank purely by how positive the carbonyl carbon is.
Trichloroacetaldehyde first: its three chlorines yank electron density away, so its carbonyl carbon is the most electron-poor and therefore the most reactive.
Methanal next: it has zero electron-pushing alkyl groups to soften the charge.
Ethanal has one electron-pushing methyl, and propanone has two plus extra steric crowding, so propanone is the least reactive.
So the order is trichloroacetaldehyde, greater than methanal, greater than ethanal, greater than propanone. Count electron-withdrawing versus electron-donating groups and you never need a calculator.
यह reactivity toward nucleophilic addition पर एक classic N E E T speed trap है, और इसे दस second के अंदर solve किया जा सकता है।
Diagram चारों molecules को इस हिसाब से rank करता है कि carbonyl carbon कितना electron-poor है; वही ranking पूरा जवाब है।
<curious> Trap यह है: students mechanically aldehyde before ketone लिखकर रुक जाते हैं, लेकिन इनमें से एक aldehyde super-charged है।
Mental shortcut यह है कि बस इस हिसाब से rank कीजिए कि carbonyl carbon कितना positive है।
Trichloroacetaldehyde पहले: इसके तीन chlorines electron density खींच लेते हैं, तो इसका carbonyl carbon सबसे electron-poor और इसलिए सबसे reactive है।
Methanal उसके बाद: इसके पास charge को soft करने के लिए कोई electron-pushing alkyl group नहीं है।
Ethanal में एक electron-pushing methyl है, और propanone में दो plus extra steric crowding, तो propanone सबसे कम reactive है।

तो order है trichloroacetaldehyde, greater than methanal, greater than ethanal, greater than propanone। Electron-withdrawing versus electron-donating groups गिनिए और calculator की ज़रूरत कभी नहीं पड़ेगी।

board_events.text: Reductive ozonolysis cleaves C=C and caps each carbon with =O.
Re-join the two carbonyl carbons to reconstruct the double bond.
Products: propanal ($CH_3CH_2CHO$) and ethanal ($CH_3CHO$).
To make propanal cleanly, avoid over-oxidation: use PCC, or Cu at $\approx 573$ K.

segments.text: This J E E Main question links three ideas at once: cleave-and-recombine logic, naming, and oxidation control. Let us walk it through.
The diagram shows the recombination trick; keep an eye on it.
Reductive ozonolysis cleaves a carbon-carbon double bond and caps each of those carbons with a double-bonded oxygen.
So to run it backwards, we simply re-join the two carbonyl carbons of the products to reconstruct the original double bond.
Joining propanal and ethanal at their carbonyl carbons gives pent-two-ene, and its formula C five H ten checks out.
The two carbonyl products are named simply: propanal and ethanal.
Now the third part: to make propanal cleanly from propan-one-ol, you must avoid over-oxidation to propanoic acid, so reach for a mild oxidant like P C C.
Alternatively, dehydrogenate the alcohol vapour over copper at about five hundred seventy three kelvin, which strips hydrogen and stops cleanly at the aldehyde.
यह J E E Main question तीन ideas को एक साथ जोड़ता है: cleave-and-recombine logic, naming, और oxidation control। चलिए इसे solve करते हैं।
Diagram recombination trick दिखाता है; उस पर नज़र रखिए।
Reductive ozonolysis एक carbon-carbon double bond को cleave करता है और उन दोनों carbons पर एक double-bonded oxygen लगा देता है।
तो इसे उल्टा चलाने के लिए, हम बस products के दो carbonyl carbons को दोबारा जोड़कर original double bond बनाते हैं।
Propanal और ethanal को उनके carbonyl carbons पर जोड़ने से pent-two-ene बनता है, और इसका formula C five H ten सही बैठता है।
दोनों carbonyl products के नाम simple हैं: propanal और ethanal।
अब तीसरा part: propan-one-ol से propanal cleanly बनाने के लिए, आपको propanoic acid तक over-oxidation से बचना है, तो P C C जैसा mild oxidant use कीजिए।
या फिर, alcohol vapour को copper पर लगभग पाँच सौ तिहत्तर kelvin पर dehydrogenate कीजिए, जो hydrogen strip करता है और aldehyde पर cleanly रुक जाता है।

board_events.text: Shared danger: $LiAlH_4$ drives both all the way to the alcohol (or amine).
Fix: DIBAL-H at low temperature delivers a single hydride and stops at a stable intermediate.
Products: pentanal (aliphatic) and benzaldehyde (aromatic).
Pentanal is more reactive: the ring donates electrons into benzaldehyde's carbonyl.

segments.text: This J E E Advanced problem tests reagent selectivity, not just reduction. The task: turn a nitrile and an ester each into its aldehyde in one operation.
The diagram shows both conversions and the reagent that makes them selective.
The shared danger is over-reduction: lithium aluminium hydride would drive both substrates all the way to the primary alcohol, or for the nitrile, to the amine, erasing the aldehyde entirely.
The fix is a bulky, low-temperature, single-delivery hydride: D I B A L-H. It delivers just one hydride and stops at a stable intermediate that only collapses to the aldehyde on aqueous work-up.
For the nitrile, D I B A L-H then water gives pentanal.
For the ester, the same reagent then water gives benzaldehyde.
So the two products are pentanal, which is aliphatic, and benzaldehyde, which is aromatic.
<whisper> Which is more reactive toward nucleophiles? Pentanal, because the benzene ring donates electron density into benzaldehyde's carbonyl by resonance, lowering its delta plus.
यह J E E Advanced problem reagent selectivity test करता है, सिर्फ़ reduction नहीं। Task: एक nitrile और एक ester को एक ही operation में उनके aldehyde में बदलना।
Diagram दोनों conversions और वह reagent दिखाता है जो इन्हें selective बनाता है।
Shared danger over-reduction है: lithium aluminium hydride दोनों substrates को पूरी तरह primary alcohol तक, या nitrile के लिए amine तक, ले जाता, aldehyde को मिटा देता।
Fix एक bulky, low-temperature, single-delivery hydride है: D I B A L-H। यह सिर्फ़ एक hydride देता है और एक stable intermediate पर रुकता है जो सिर्फ़ aqueous work-up पर aldehyde में बदलता है।
Nitrile के लिए, D I B A L-H फिर water pentanal देता है।
Ester के लिए, वही reagent फिर water benzaldehyde देता है।
तो दो products हैं pentanal, जो aliphatic है, और benzaldehyde, जो aromatic है।
<whisper> कौन ज़्यादा reactive है nucleophiles के लिए? Pentanal, क्योंकि benzene ring resonance से benzaldehyde के carbonyl में electron density donate करता है, उसका delta plus कम कर देता है।

board_events.text: Where marks quietly leak away
Never put a locant on the aldehyde group: it is C-1 by definition (AK-NOM-01).
Number a ketone for the lowest locant — pentan-2-one, never pentan-4-one (AK-NOM-02).
The aldehyde-over-ketone rule assumes ordinary alkyls: $CCl_3CHO$ outranks them; aromatics are de-activated (AK-STR-01).
Match a named reaction to its substrate: Rosenmund needs an acyl chloride, not a nitrile (AK-PREP-01).
Pro-tip: for reactivity, run a 5-second charge audit — count $-I$ pullers versus $+I$ pushers.
For 'make an aldehyde', the reflex is a gentle reagent: Rosenmund's poison or cold DIBAL-H (AK-PREP-02).
The examiner is almost always testing whether you can avoid over-reduction.

segments.text: Let us close the sub-topic with the pitfalls that quietly cost marks, and the reflexes that save them.
First and most common: never put a locant on the aldehyde group. The C H O carbon is carbon one by definition, so propan-one-al and butan-one-al are both wrong.
Second: always number a ketone to give the carbonyl the lowest locant. Check both ends before you commit, so pentan-two-one, never pentan-four-one.

Third: the aldehyde-beats-ketone rule assumes ordinary alkyl groups. Trichloroacetaldehyde outranks them, and aromatic carbonyls are de-activated by the ring, so decide by reasoning about the delta plus.

Fourth: match each named reaction to its substrate. Rosenmund needs an acyl chloride, Stephen and D I B A L-H act on nitriles, and dialkylcadmium makes ketones. Memorise the substrate, not just the name.
Pro-tip for reactivity questions: run a five-second charge audit, counting electron-withdrawing pullers, which raise reactivity, against electron-donating pushers, which lower it.
And the preparation reflex: whenever the answer must be an aldehyde, reach for a gentle, selective reagent, Rosenmund's poisoned catalyst or D I B A L-H in the cold.
Because in these preparation questions the examiner is almost always testing one thing: whether you can avoid over-reduction.
चलिए sub-topic को उन pitfalls के साथ बंद करते हैं जो चुपके से marks ले जाते हैं, और उन reflexes के साथ जो उन्हें बचाते हैं।
पहला और सबसे common: aldehyde group पर कभी locant मत लगाइए। C H O carbon by definition carbon one है, तो propan-one-al और butan-one-al दोनों ग़लत हैं।
दूसरा: ketone को हमेशा ऐसे number कीजिए कि carbonyl को सबसे छोटा locant मिले। Commit करने से पहले दोनों ends check कीजिए, तो pentan-two-one, कभी pentan-four-one नहीं।

तीसरा: aldehyde-beats-ketone rule ordinary alkyl groups मानता है। Trichloroacetaldehyde इनसे आगे है, और aromatic carbonyls ring से de-activated होते हैं, तो delta plus के बारे में सोच कर decide कीजिए।

चौथा: हर named reaction को उसके substrate से match कीजिए। Rosenmund को acyl chloride चाहिए, Stephen और D I B A L-H nitriles पर काम करते हैं, और dialkylcadmium ketones बनाता है। Substrate याद रखिए, सिर्फ़ नाम नहीं।
Reactivity questions के लिए pro-tip: एक five-second charge audit चलाइए, electron-withdrawing pullers जो reactivity बढ़ाते हैं, versus electron-donating pushers जो इसे घटाते हैं, गिनकर।
और preparation reflex: जब भी answer aldehyde होना हो, एक gentle, selective reagent उठाइए, Rosenmund का poisoned catalyst या ठंडे में D I B A L-H।
क्योंकि इन preparation questions में examiner लगभग हमेशा एक ही चीज़ test करता है: क्या आप over-reduction से बच सकते हैं।

board_events.text: Front counter — the carbonyl carbon ($\delta+$): electron-rich nucleophiles attack here.
This one move, nucleophilic addition, is the parent of cyanohydrins, acetals, imines, Grignard products and reduction.
Back counter — the $\alpha$-carbon next door: its hydrogens are unusually acidic.
Remove an $\alpha$-H and the charge slides onto oxygen as a resonance-stabilised enolate.
The enolate is itself a nucleophile, so it attacks another carbonyl — that is the aldol reaction.
Separately, the lone H on an aldehyde makes aldehydes easy to oxidise — the basis of every 'distinguish' test.
No $\alpha$-H (benzaldehyde, methanal, trimethylacetaldehyde)? Aldol is off and Cannizzaro takes over.

segments.text: <curious> Before any single reaction, grasp the big picture: an aldehyde or ketone is not a one-trick molecule, it has two distinct reactive sites.
Picture the carbonyl as a small shop with two service counters, shown here.
The front counter is the carbonyl carbon itself. It is electron-poor, delta plus, so electron-rich nucleophiles walk up and attack it.
That single move, nucleophilic addition, is the parent of cyanohydrin formation, acetals, imines, Grignard addition and reduction. They look like a zoo, but mechanically they are siblings.
The back counter is the alpha-carbon, the carbon right next to the carbonyl, and its hydrogens are unusually acidic.
Why acidic? Because once a base plucks an alpha-H off, the leftover negative charge does not sit on carbon, it slides onto the electronegative oxygen through resonance, giving a stabilised enolate.
That enolate is itself a nucleophile, so it can march over and attack the front counter of another molecule. That is exactly the aldol reaction.
One more theme: the lone hydrogen on an aldehyde's carbonyl carbon makes aldehydes easy to oxidise to acids, which is the basis of nearly every distinguish-A-from-B test.
<whisper> And the flip side: if there is no alpha-H at all, as in benzaldehyde, methanal or trimethylacetaldehyde, aldol is impossible and the Cannizzaro route takes over under strong alkali.
<curious> किसी भी single reaction से पहले बड़ी picture समझिए: एक aldehyde या ketone one-trick molecule नहीं है, इसके दो अलग reactive sites होते हैं।
Carbonyl को एक छोटी दुकान की तरह सोचिए जिसमें दो service counters हैं, जैसा यहाँ दिखाया गया है।
Front counter खुद carbonyl carbon है। यह electron-poor है, delta plus, इसलिए electron-rich nucleophiles इसे attack करते हैं।
वही एक move, nucleophilic addition, cyanohydrin formation, acetals, imines, Grignard addition और reduction का parent है। ये अलग-अलग लगते हैं, पर mechanically siblings हैं।
Back counter alpha-carbon है, carbonyl के बिलकुल बगल वाला carbon, और इसके hydrogens unusually acidic होते हैं।
Acidic क्यों? क्योंकि जब base एक alpha-H हटा देता है, बची हुई negative charge carbon पर नहीं रुकती, वह resonance से electronegative oxygen पर slide हो जाती है, एक stabilised enolate देती है।
वह enolate खुद एक nucleophile है, तो वह दूसरे molecule के front counter पर attack कर सकता है। यही बिलकुल aldol reaction है।
एक और theme: aldehyde के carbonyl carbon पर lone hydrogen aldehydes को acids तक easily oxidise करवा देता है, जो लगभग हर distinguish-A-from-B test का basis है।
<whisper> और उल्टा पहलू: अगर कोई alpha-H है ही नहीं, जैसे benzaldehyde, methanal या trimethylacetaldehyde में, तो aldol impossible है और strong alkali में Cannizzaro route संभाल लेता है।

board_events.text: 1. Attack: $Nu^-$ approaches the carbonyl carbon perpendicular to the $sp^2$ plane, into the $\pi^*$.
2. Rehybridise: the carbon flips $sp^2 \to sp^3$ and the $\pi$ electrons collapse onto oxygen.
3. Protonate: the tetrahedral alkoxide grabs a proton, giving the neutral product.
Net result: $Nu$ and $H$ add across the C=O double bond.
Weak nucleophiles (ammonia derivatives) need a trace of acid first to protonate the oxygen and boost the carbon.
That is why those reactions run best near $\text{pH } 3.5$ — acidic enough to activate, not so acidic it kills the amine.

segments.text: Learn this one mechanism properly and roughly a dozen reactions simply fall out of it.
Follow the three stages in the diagram.
Stage one, attack: a nucleophile approaches the carbonyl carbon from roughly perpendicular to the flat s p two plane and donates a lone pair into the empty pi-star of the carbon-oxygen bond.
Stage two, rehybridisation: as the new carbon-nucleophile bond forms, the carbon changes from s p two to s p three and the pi electrons collapse onto oxygen, giving a tetrahedral alkoxide.
Stage three, protonation: that alkoxide simply grabs a proton from the medium to give the neutral product.
In symbols: carbonyl, plus nucleophile, gives an alkoxide with the nucleophile attached, then plus a proton gives the hydroxyl product.
So the net result is that the nucleophile and a hydrogen add across the carbon-oxygen double bond.
One refinement: weak nucleophiles, like the ammonia derivatives coming up, need a trace of acid first, which protonates the carbonyl oxygen and makes the carbon even more electrophilic.
<whisper> That is why those particular reactions run best near p H three point five, acidic enough to activate the carbonyl, but not so acidic that it protonates and disables the amine itself.
इस एक mechanism को ठीक से सीख लीजिए और लगभग एक dozen reactions इसी से निकल आती हैं।
Diagram में तीन stages follow कीजिए।
Stage एक, attack: एक nucleophile carbonyl carbon के पास लगभग flat s p two plane के perpendicular से आता है और अपना lone pair carbon-oxygen bond के खाली pi-star में donate करता है।
Stage दो, rehybridisation: जैसे नया carbon-nucleophile bond बनता है, carbon s p two से s p three हो जाता है और pi electrons oxygen पर collapse हो जाते हैं, एक tetrahedral alkoxide देते हैं।
Stage तीन, protonation: वह alkoxide बस medium से एक proton पकड़ कर neutral product दे देता है।
Symbols में: carbonyl, plus nucleophile, एक alkoxide देता है जिसमें nucleophile जुड़ा है, फिर plus एक proton hydroxyl product देता है।
तो net result यह है कि nucleophile और एक hydrogen carbon-oxygen double bond के आर-पार add हो जाते हैं।
एक refinement: weak nucleophiles, जैसे आगे आने वाले ammonia derivatives, को पहले थोड़ा acid चाहिए, जो carbonyl oxygen को protonate करके carbon को और electrophilic बना देता है।
<whisper> इसी वजह से वो खास reactions p H three point five के पास best चलती हैं, इतना acidic कि carbonyl activate हो, पर इतना नहीं कि amine खुद protonate होकर बेकार हो जाए।

board_events.text: $HCN$ (base-catalysed) adds to give a cyanohydrin — a handy synthetic intermediate.
$NaHSO_3$ gives a crystalline bisulphite adduct.
The bisulphite adduct is reversible: regenerate the carbonyl with dilute acid or alkali — used to purify aldehydes.
$RMgX$ then aqueous acid gives an alcohol: $1^\circ$ from methanal, $2^\circ$ from other aldehydes, $3^\circ$ from ketones.
An alcohol with dry $HCl$ gives a hemiacetal, then an acetal (a $gem$-dialkoxy).
Acetal formation is reversible, so acetals are used as a protecting group for the carbonyl.
Aldehydes, being more reactive, form these adducts more readily than ketones.

segments.text: Now the family of additions. They share the mechanism you just learned, and each gives a product examiners love.
The hub-and-spoke diagram shows four of them fanning out from one carbonyl.
First, hydrogen cyanide, base-catalysed so the true nucleophile is the cyanide ion, adds to give a cyanohydrin, a useful synthetic intermediate.
Second, sodium bisulphite gives a crystalline bisulphite addition compound.
This one is special because it is reversible: treat it with dilute acid or alkali and you get the pure carbonyl back. That is exactly how chemists pull an aldehyde out of a mixture and purify it.
Third, a Grignard reagent followed by aqueous acid gives an alcohol, and the class depends on the carbonyl: a primary alcohol from methanal, secondary from other aldehydes, tertiary from ketones.
Fourth, an alcohol with dry hydrogen chloride first gives a hemiacetal and then an acetal, a carbon bearing two alkoxy groups.

<excited> And here is the clever bit: acetal formation is fully reversible, so chemists use acetals as a protecting group, hiding a reactive aldehyde while they work elsewhere in the molecule, then unmasking it.
Across all four, aldehydes, being more reactive, form these adducts more readily than ketones, exactly mirroring the reactivity order from the last sub-topic.
अब additions की family। ये वही mechanism share करती हैं जो आपने अभी सीखा, और हर एक ऐसा product देती है जो examiners को पसंद है।
Hub-and-spoke diagram इनमें से चार को एक carbonyl से फैलते हुए दिखाता है।
पहला, hydrogen cyanide, base-catalysed ताकि असली nucleophile cyanide ion हो, add होकर एक cyanohydrin देता है, एक useful synthetic intermediate।
दूसरा, sodium bisulphite एक crystalline bisulphite addition compound देता है।
यह खास है क्योंकि reversible है: इसे dilute acid या alkali से treat कीजिए और pure carbonyl वापस मिल जाता है। Chemists इसी तरह mixture से aldehyde निकाल कर purify करते हैं।
तीसरा, एक Grignard reagent फिर aqueous acid एक alcohol देता है, और उसकी class carbonyl पर depend करती है: methanal से primary, दूसरे aldehydes से secondary, ketones से tertiary।
चौथा, एक alcohol dry hydrogen chloride के साथ पहले एक hemiacetal और फिर एक acetal देता है, एक carbon जिसपर दो alkoxy groups हैं।

<excited> और यह रही clever बात: acetal formation पूरी तरह reversible है, इसलिए chemists acetals को protecting group की तरह use करते हैं, एक reactive aldehyde को छुपा कर जब तक molecule में कहीं और काम करते हैं, फिर उसे unmask कर लेते हैं।
चारों में, aldehydes, ज़्यादा reactive होने की वजह से, ये adducts ketones से आसानी से बनाते हैं, जो पिछले sub-topic के reactivity order को बिलकुल mirror करता है।

board_events.text: A reagent $H_2N{-}Z$ adds to the carbonyl; the adduct then loses water to give $>\!C{=}N{-}Z$.
Ammonia $\to$ imine; a $1^\circ$ amine $\to$ substituted imine (Schiff base).
Hydroxylamine $\to$ oxime; hydrazine $\to$ hydrazone; phenylhydrazine $\to$ phenylhydrazone.
Semicarbazide $\to$ semicarbazone; note $NH_2$ of the amide part is un-reactive, so only one end adds.
Brady's reagent, 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine, gives a yellow-to-red solid.
2,4-DNP is positive for any carbonyl — aldehyde or ketone — so it characterises, it does not distinguish.
These weak nucleophiles are exactly why the reaction is acid-catalysed near $\text{pH } 3.5$.

segments.text: This whole family runs on one template: add a nitrogen nucleophile across the carbonyl, then eliminate water to leave a carbon-nitrogen double bond.
The diagram is one reaction with a swappable group Z; change Z and you change the product's name.
The general reagent is written H two N dash Z. It adds to the carbonyl, then the adduct loses water to give a carbon double bond nitrogen dash Z.
When Z is just hydrogen, from ammonia, you get an imine; from a primary amine you get a substituted imine, called a Schiff base.
Hydroxylamine gives an oxime, hydrazine gives a hydrazone, and phenylhydrazine gives a phenylhydrazone.
Semicarbazide gives a semicarbazone; interestingly only one of its nitrogen ends is nucleophilic, the amide nitrogen stays out, so the product is clean.
Brady's reagent, two comma four-dinitrophenylhydrazine, gives a coloured solid from yellow through orange to red.

<whisper> But here is the exam trap: the two comma four-D N P test is positive for any carbonyl, aldehyde or ketone alike, so it characterises a carbonyl, it can never distinguish an aldehyde from a ketone.
And because all these nitrogen nucleophiles are weak, this is exactly the family that needs mild acid catalysis near p H three point five.
यह पूरी family एक template पर चलती है: एक nitrogen nucleophile carbonyl के आर-पार add कीजिए, फिर water eliminate करके एक carbon-nitrogen double bond छोड़ दीजिए।
Diagram एक reaction है जिसमें एक बदलने वाला group Z है; Z बदलिए और product का नाम बदल जाता है।
General reagent H two N dash Z लिखा जाता है। यह carbonyl पर add होता है, फिर adduct water खो कर एक carbon double bond nitrogen dash Z देता है।
जब Z सिर्फ hydrogen हो, ammonia से, तो imine मिलता है; primary amine से substituted imine मिलता है, जिसे Schiff base कहते हैं।
Hydroxylamine oxime देता है, hydrazine hydrazone देता है, और phenylhydrazine phenylhydrazone देता है।
Semicarbazide semicarbazone देता है; दिलचस्प बात, इसके सिर्फ एक nitrogen end nucleophilic है, amide nitrogen अलग रहता है, इसलिए product clean होता है।
Brady's reagent, two comma four-dinitrophenylhydrazine, एक coloured solid देता है, yellow से orange से red तक।

<whisper> पर यहाँ exam trap है: two comma four-D N P test किसी भी carbonyl के लिए positive है, aldehyde हो या ketone, इसलिए यह carbonyl को characterise करता है, aldehyde और ketone को कभी distinguish नहीं कर सकता।
और क्योंकि ये सारे nitrogen nucleophiles weak हैं, यही वह family है जिसे p H three point five के पास mild acid catalysis चाहिए।

board_events.text: To alcohols: $NaBH_4$, $LiAlH_4$ or $H_2$/Ni — aldehyde $\to 1^\circ$, ketone $\to 2^\circ$.
Selectivity: $LiAlH_4$ also hits esters and acid chlorides; $NaBH_4$ is milder and leaves them alone.
Catalytic $H_2$ also reduces any C=C double bonds — watch for that in unsaturated substrates.
To hydrocarbons ($>\!C{=}O \to >\!CH_2$): Clemmensen and Wolff–Kishner remove the oxygen entirely.
Choose by medium: acid-sensitive group $\Rightarrow$ Wolff–Kishner; base-sensitive group $\Rightarrow$ Clemmensen.

segments.text: Reduction of a carbonyl comes in two depths, and choosing between them is really about the reaction medium.
The diagram splits shallow from deep.
Shallow first: to alcohols, using sodium borohydride, lithium aluminium hydride, or hydrogen over nickel. An aldehyde becomes a primary alcohol, a ketone a secondary alcohol.
Selectivity matters here: lithium aluminium hydride is powerful and also reduces esters and acid chlorides, whereas sodium borohydride is milder and leaves those, and nitro groups, untouched.
And remember catalytic hydrogen also reduces carbon-carbon double bonds, so in an unsaturated substrate it is not selective for the carbonyl.
Now the deep reduction, all the way to a hydrocarbon: carbonyl to a C H two group, removing the oxygen entirely. Two named methods do this.
Clemmensen uses zinc amalgam with concentrated hydrochloric acid, so it runs in acidic medium.
Wolff-Kishner uses hydrazine, then potassium hydroxide in glycol heated to about one hundred eighty to two hundred degrees Celsius, so it runs in basic medium.
<whisper> So the decision is purely about the medium: if the molecule has an acid-sensitive group, use Wolff-Kishner; if it has a base-sensitive group, use Clemmensen.
Carbonyl का reduction दो depths में आता है, और इनमें choose करना असल में reaction medium के बारे में है।
Diagram shallow को deep से अलग करता है।
पहले shallow: alcohols तक, sodium borohydride, lithium aluminium hydride, या hydrogen over nickel से। एक aldehyde primary alcohol बनता है, एक ketone secondary alcohol।
यहाँ selectivity important है: lithium aluminium hydride powerful है और esters और acid chlorides को भी reduce करता है, जबकि sodium borohydride milder है और उन्हें, और nitro groups को, छोड़ देता है।
और याद रखिए catalytic hydrogen carbon-carbon double bonds को भी reduce करता है, तो unsaturated substrate में वह carbonyl के लिए selective नहीं है।
अब deep reduction, पूरी तरह hydrocarbon तक: carbonyl से एक C H two group, oxygen को पूरी तरह हटा कर। दो named methods यह करती हैं।
Clemmensen zinc amalgam को concentrated hydrochloric acid के साथ use करता है, तो यह acidic medium में चलता है।
Wolff-Kishner hydrazine, फिर glycol में potassium hydroxide को लगभग one hundred eighty to two hundred degrees Celsius पर use करता है, तो यह basic medium में चलता है।
<whisper> तो decision पूरी तरह medium के बारे में है: अगर molecule में acid-sensitive group है, Wolff-Kishner use कीजिए; अगर base-sensitive group है, Clemmensen use कीजिए।

board_events.text: Oxidising an aldehyde only swaps its C–H for a C–OH — a gentle, low-barrier change.
A ketone has no carbonyl H; oxidation must break a strong C–C bond, so mild reagents fail.
Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal $AgNO_3$) $\to$ a silver mirror for aldehydes.
Fehling's / Benedict's $\to$ a red-brown $Cu_2O$ precipitate — but only for aliphatic aldehydes.
Benzaldehyde does not respond to Fehling's; and remember 'the aldehyde reduces the reagent'.
Strong oxidants ($KMnO_4$, $K_2Cr_2O_7$) push an aldehyde all the way to a carboxylic acid.
A carbonyl with $\alpha$-H also exists in equilibrium with a little enol — the key to the next reactions.

segments.text: Now oxidation, and the whole set of tests that distinguish an aldehyde from a ketone rests on one structural fact.
The two-panel diagram shows aldehydes reacting and ketones sitting inert.
Oxidising an aldehyde only requires swapping its carbonyl carbon-hydrogen bond for a carbon-hydroxyl. That is a gentle, low-barrier change even a mild oxidant can drive.
A ketone has no such hydrogen on the carbonyl carbon; to oxidise it you must break a strong carbon-carbon bond, which mild reagents simply cannot do, so ketones do not respond.
So Tollens' reagent, which is ammoniacal silver nitrate, is reduced by an aldehyde to metallic silver, depositing a bright silver mirror.
Fehling's and Benedict's give a red-brown cuprous oxide precipitate, but with an important caveat: they work only for aliphatic aldehydes.
Benzaldehyde, an aromatic aldehyde, does not respond to Fehling's. And read the direction carefully: the aldehyde reduces the reagent while being oxidised itself.
If instead you use a strong oxidant like potassium permanganate or potassium dichromate, the aldehyde is driven all the way to a carboxylic acid.

<curious> One more structural idea to carry forward: a carbonyl with an alpha-H sits in equilibrium with a small amount of its enol form, and that enol is the doorway into the reactions we tackle next.
अब oxidation, और aldehyde को ketone से distinguish करने वाले सारे tests एक structural fact पर टिके हैं।
दो-panel diagram aldehydes को react करते और ketones को inert बैठे दिखाता है।
एक aldehyde को oxidise करने के लिए बस उसके carbonyl carbon-hydrogen bond को carbon-hydroxyl से बदलना होता है। यह एक gentle, low-barrier change है जिसे mild oxidant भी कर सकता है।
Ketone में carbonyl carbon पर ऐसा कोई hydrogen नहीं है; इसे oxidise करने के लिए एक strong carbon-carbon bond तोड़ना पड़ेगा, जो mild reagents नहीं कर सकते, इसलिए ketones respond नहीं करते।
तो Tollens' reagent, जो ammoniacal silver nitrate है, aldehyde द्वारा metallic silver में reduce हो जाता है, एक चमकता silver mirror जमा करता है।
Fehling's और Benedict's एक red-brown cuprous oxide precipitate देते हैं, पर एक important caveat के साथ: ये सिर्फ aliphatic aldehydes के लिए काम करते हैं।
Benzaldehyde, एक aromatic aldehyde, Fehling's को respond नहीं करता। और direction ध्यान से पढ़िए: aldehyde reagent को reduce करता है जबकि खुद oxidise होता है।
अगर इसकी जगह आप potassium permanganate या potassium dichromate जैसा strong oxidant use करें, तो aldehyde पूरी तरह carboxylic acid तक चला जाता है।
<curious> एक और structural idea आगे ले जाइए: alpha-H वाला carbonyl अपने enol form के थोड़े amount के साथ equilibrium में रहता है, और वही enol अगले reactions का दरवाज़ा है।

board_events.text: 1. A base removes an $\alpha$-H to give the resonance-stabilised enolate.
2. The enolate attacks a second carbonyl carbon — mechanism 3A with the enolate as $Nu$.
3. Protonation gives the aldol: a $\beta$-hydroxy aldehyde or ketone.
On heating the aldol loses water; conjugation with C=O is the driving force $\to$ an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated carbonyl.
Cross-aldol of two different $\alpha$-H carbonyls gives four products — a messy mixture.
It is clean only when one partner has no $\alpha$-H (benzaldehyde): it is locked as the electrophile.

segments.text: Now the back-counter chemistry: the aldol reaction, where an enolate builds a brand-new carbon-carbon bond.
Track the steps in the diagram using ethanal as the example.
Step one: a base removes an alpha-hydrogen to give the carbanion, which is resonance-stabilised as the enolate, with charge delocalised onto oxygen.
Step two: that enolate, being a nucleophile, attacks the carbonyl carbon of a second molecule. This is just the master addition mechanism with the enolate playing the nucleophile.
Step three: protonation gives the aldol itself, a beta-hydroxy aldehyde or ketone.
For ethanal: two molecules give three-hydroxybutanal, which on heating gives but-two-enal, also called crotonaldehyde.
That heating step is the condensation: the aldol loses water, and the driving force is that the new double bond ends up conjugated with the carbonyl, giving an alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl.

Now a warning about cross-aldol: mix two different carbonyls that both have alpha-H, and either can be the enolate and either the electrophile, so you get four products, a mixture that is hard to separate.

<whisper> It becomes clean and useful only when one partner has no alpha-H, such as benzaldehyde. That partner cannot form an enolate, so it is locked into the electrophile role, and benzaldehyde plus ethanal cleanly gives cinnamaldehyde.
अब back-counter chemistry: aldol reaction, जहाँ एक enolate एक बिलकुल नया carbon-carbon bond बनाता है।
Diagram में ethanal को example लेकर steps track कीजिए।
Step एक: एक base एक alpha-hydrogen हटा कर carbanion देता है, जो enolate के रूप में resonance-stabilised है, charge oxygen पर delocalised।
Step दो: वह enolate, nucleophile होने की वजह से, दूसरे molecule के carbonyl carbon पर attack करता है। यह बस master addition mechanism है जिसमें enolate nucleophile का role निभा रहा है।
Step तीन: protonation aldol खुद देता है, एक beta-hydroxy aldehyde या ketone।
Ethanal के लिए: दो molecules three-hydroxybutanal देते हैं, जो heat करने पर but-two-enal देता है, जिसे crotonaldehyde भी कहते हैं।
वह heating step condensation है: aldol water खो देता है, और driving force यह है कि नया double bond carbonyl के साथ conjugated हो जाता है, एक alpha,beta-unsaturated carbonyl देता है।

अब cross-aldol की warning: दो अलग carbonyls मिलाइए जिनमें दोनों के पास alpha-H हो, और कोई भी enolate और कोई भी electrophile बन सकता है, तो चार products मिलते हैं, एक mixture जिसे separate करना मुश्किल है।

<whisper> यह clean और useful तभी बनता है जब एक partner के पास alpha-H ना हो, जैसे benzaldehyde। वह partner enolate बना ही नहीं सकता, इसलिए electrophile role में lock हो जाता है, और benzaldehyde plus ethanal cleanly cinnamaldehyde देता है।

board_events.text: Only aldehydes with no $\alpha$-H, under concentrated alkali, take this route.
1. Hydroxide adds to the carbonyl carbon, giving a tetrahedral alkoxide (addition with $Nu = OH^-$).
2. That intermediate transfers a hydride ion to a second aldehyde molecule.
Donor $\to$ carboxylate (oxidised); acceptor $\to$ alcohol (reduced) — self oxidation–reduction.
Decision tree: $\alpha$-H present $\to$ aldol; no $\alpha$-H $\to$ Cannizzaro.
An aldehyde that has $\alpha$-H reacts by aldol far faster, so it never gives Cannizzaro.

segments.text: Cannizzaro is the reaction reserved for aldehydes that cannot do aldol, because they have no alpha-hydrogen.
The diagram shows both the mechanism and the decision tree that tells you which reaction to expect.
The condition is strict: only an aldehyde with no alpha-H, under concentrated alkali, takes this route.
Step one: hydroxide ion adds to the carbonyl carbon, giving a tetrahedral alkoxide. That is just our master addition with hydroxide as the nucleophile.
Step two: that intermediate transfers a hydride ion across to the carbonyl carbon of a second aldehyde molecule.
The consequence is beautiful: the donor becomes a carboxylate, that is oxidised, while the acceptor becomes an alcohol, that is reduced. One reaction, opposite fates, a self oxidation-reduction.
For methanal: two molecules under concentrated sodium hydroxide give methanol plus sodium formate.
So the decision tree for any such question is simple: alpha-H present means aldol; no alpha-H means Cannizzaro under concentrated alkali.
<whisper> And note the one-way door: an aldehyde that does have alpha-H reacts by aldol far faster than by Cannizzaro, so it will never give the Cannizzaro product.
Cannizzaro वह reaction है जो उन aldehydes के लिए reserved है जो aldol नहीं कर सकते, क्योंकि उनके पास alpha-hydrogen नहीं है।
Diagram mechanism और decision tree दोनों दिखाता है जो बताता है कि कौन सी reaction expect करनी है।
Condition strict है: सिर्फ एक aldehyde जिसके पास alpha-H ना हो, concentrated alkali में, यह route लेता है।
Step एक: hydroxide ion carbonyl carbon पर add होता है, एक tetrahedral alkoxide देता है। यह बस हमारा master addition है जिसमें hydroxide nucleophile है।
Step दो: वह intermediate एक hydride ion दूसरे aldehyde molecule के carbonyl carbon पर transfer कर देता है।
नतीजा खूबसूरत है: donor carboxylate बन जाता है, वह oxidise होता है, जबकि acceptor alcohol बन जाता है, वह reduce होता है। एक reaction, उल्टे अंजाम, एक self oxidation-reduction।
Methanal के लिए: दो molecules concentrated sodium hydroxide में methanol plus sodium formate देते हैं।
तो ऐसे किसी भी सवाल का decision tree simple है: alpha-H present मतलब aldol; कोई alpha-H नहीं मतलब concentrated alkali में Cannizzaro।
<whisper> और एक-तरफा दरवाज़ा ध्यान में रखिए: जिस aldehyde के पास alpha-H है वह Cannizzaro से कहीं तेज़ aldol करता है, इसलिए वह कभी Cannizzaro product नहीं देगा।

A $CH_3CH(OH)$– group also passes, because alkali first oxidises it to the $CH_3CO$– unit.
So the test flags a substructure, not one molecule: ethanal and ethanol both test positive.
Acetone tests positive; pentan-3-one and propan-1-ol test negative.
It is an $\alpha$-H reaction: the acidic methyl hydrogens are what get sequentially halogenated.
Pair it with Tollens' to separate a methyl ketone from a methyl-bearing aldehyde.

segments.text: The iodoform test is a NEET and boards favourite because a single yellow precipitate reveals a specific piece of structure.
The diagram shows exactly which fragment triggers it.
A methyl-carbonyl group, written C H three C O dash, treated with iodine in sodium hydroxide, gives yellow iodoform as a precipitate plus a carboxylate.
In symbols: the methyl ketone, under iodine and sodium hydroxide, gives iodoform, which precipitates, plus the carboxylate.
Crucially, a C H three C H with an O H group also passes, because the alkali first oxidises that alcohol to the methyl-carbonyl unit.
So the test flags a substructure rather than a single compound: ethanal and ethanol both test positive, the first because it is a methyl carbonyl, the second because it oxidises to one.
Acetone tests positive because it carries a methyl carbonyl; but pentan-three-one, whose carbonyl has no methyl directly attached, and propan-one-ol test negative.
Mechanistically it is an alpha-H reaction: the acidic methyl hydrogens are the ones that get halogenated one after another before the carbon-carbon bond finally breaks.
<whisper> Pair the iodoform test with Tollens', and you can cleanly separate a methyl ketone, which fails Tollens', from a methyl-bearing aldehyde like ethanal, which passes both.

एक methyl-carbonyl group, जिसे C H three C O dash लिखते हैं, sodium hydroxide में iodine के साथ treat करने पर, yellow iodoform एक precipitate के रूप में plus एक carboxylate देता है।

खास बात, एक C H three C H जिसमें O H group हो वह भी pass करता है, क्योंकि alkali पहले उस alcohol को methyl-carbonyl unit में oxidise कर देता है।
तो test एक substructure को flag करता है, एक single compound को नहीं: ethanal और ethanol दोनों positive test देते हैं, पहला क्योंकि वह methyl carbonyl है, दूसरा क्योंकि वह उसमें oxidise हो जाता है।

Mechanically यह एक alpha-H reaction है: acidic methyl hydrogens ही एक के बाद एक halogenate होते हैं, फिर आखिर में carbon-carbon bond टूट जाता है।

segments.text: This C B S E-style question sends one aldehyde down three different roads, and each answer follows from its structure.
The diagram routes butanal three ways at once.
First fix the key facts: butanal is an aliphatic aldehyde and it has alpha-hydrogens. Those two facts decide all three products.
Part one, Tollens' reagent: being an aldehyde, butanal reduces it to a silver mirror while being oxidised itself to butanoic acid.
Part two, dilute sodium hydroxide then heat: because butanal has alpha-H, it undergoes aldol condensation.
Two molecules combine and, on heating, lose water to give two-ethylhex-two-enal, an alpha,beta-unsaturated aldehyde.
Part three, semicarbazide in weak acid: this is addition-elimination, giving the semicarbazone.
The full-marks habit is to name the reaction type first and then the named product, rather than just scribbling a formula.
यह C B S E-style question एक aldehyde को तीन अलग रास्तों पर भेजता है, और हर जवाब उसके structure से निकलता है।

Part एक, Tollens' reagent: aldehyde होने की वजह से, butanal इसे silver mirror में reduce करता है जबकि खुद butanoic acid में oxidise होता है।
Part दो, dilute sodium hydroxide फिर heat: क्योंकि butanal के पास alpha-H है, वह aldol condensation करता है।
दो molecules जुड़ कर, heat पर, water खो कर two-ethylhex-two-enal देते हैं, एक alpha,beta-unsaturated aldehyde।
Part तीन, weak acid में semicarbazide: यह addition-elimination है, जो semicarbazone देता है।
Full-marks की आदत यह है कि पहले reaction type का नाम लिखिए, फिर named product, सिर्फ एक formula घसीटने के बजाय।

Ethanal: is a methyl carbonyl (iodoform yes) and is an aldehyde (Tollens yes).
Propan-1-ol: neither; pentan-3-one: no methyl on the carbonyl and no $-CHO$ — both fail.

segments.text: This is a NEET speed trap that rewards reading the question exactly: it wants the compound that is positive on two tests at once.
The table in the diagram scores each candidate against both filters.
<curious> Here is the trap: students remember iodoform equals methyl ketone and stop, or Tollens equals aldehyde and stop, but the question asks for the intersection of the two.
So set the two conditions clearly: the iodoform test needs a methyl-carbonyl or a methyl-with-hydroxyl unit, while Tollens needs an aldehyde group.
Take propan-two-one: it has the methyl carbonyl, so iodoform is yes, but it has no aldehyde group, so Tollens is no.
Take ethanal: it is a methyl carbonyl, so iodoform is yes, and it is an aldehyde, so Tollens is yes as well. That satisfies both.
For contrast, propan-one-ol triggers neither, and pentan-three-one has no methyl directly on the carbonyl and no aldehyde group, so both fail.
So the answer is ethanal, the classic passes-both-filters molecule you should recognise on sight.
यह एक N E E T speed trap है जो सवाल को ठीक से पढ़ने पर reward देता है: इसे वह compound चाहिए जो एक साथ दो tests पर positive हो।

$LiAlH_4$ is wrong twice: it only reaches an alcohol, and it attacks the ester.
Clemmensen runs in strong acid — it risks hydrolysing the ester.
Wolff–Kishner runs in strong base — it risks saponifying the ester.

segments.text: This J E E Advanced problem is not really about reduction, it is about whether the reducing medium is compatible with the rest of the molecule.
The diagram shows both classic deoxygenations clashing with the ester.
The target is to turn the ketone carbonyl into a C H two group while leaving the ethyl ester completely intact.
First rule out lithium aluminium hydride: it fails twice, because it only reduces the ketone as far as an alcohol, not to C H two, and it also attacks and reduces the ester.
Clemmensen runs in strongly acidic medium, so it risks hydrolysing the acid-sensitive ester.
Wolff-Kishner runs in strongly basic medium, so it risks saponifying, that is base-hydrolysing, the ester.

So neither classic method cleanly preserves an ordinary ester. The safe laboratory strategy is to protect the ketone first, for example as its cyclic ethylene-glycol ketal, carry out the transformation, then deprotect.

<whisper> The teaching point the examiner is testing is a habit: always check that the medium of a reduction, acidic Clemmensen versus basic Wolff-Kishner, is compatible with every other functional group present.
यह J E E Advanced problem असल में reduction के बारे में नहीं है, यह इस बारे में है कि reducing medium बाकी molecule के साथ compatible है या नहीं।
Diagram दोनों classic deoxygenations को ester से clash करते दिखाता है।
Target है ketone carbonyl को एक C H two group में बदलना जबकि ethyl ester को पूरी तरह intact छोड़ना।
पहले lithium aluminium hydride को rule out कीजिए: यह दो बार fail होता है, क्योंकि वह ketone को सिर्फ alcohol तक reduce करता है, C H two तक नहीं, और ester पर भी attack करके उसे reduce करता है।
Clemmensen strongly acidic medium में चलता है, तो वह acid-sensitive ester को hydrolyse करने का risk रखता है।
Wolff-Kishner strongly basic medium में चलता है, तो वह ester को saponify, यानी base-hydrolyse, करने का risk रखता है।

तो कोई भी classic method एक ordinary ester को cleanly preserve नहीं करता। Safe laboratory strategy यह है कि ketone को पहले protect कीजिए, जैसे इसके cyclic ethylene-glycol ketal के रूप में, transformation कीजिए, फिर deprotect कीजिए।

<whisper> Examiner जो teaching point test कर रहा है वह एक आदत है: हमेशा check कीजिए कि reduction का medium, acidic Clemmensen versus basic Wolff-Kishner, molecule में मौजूद हर दूसरे functional group के साथ compatible है।

board_events.text: Where reactions questions quietly go wrong
Count $\alpha$-H from the $\alpha$-carbon, never from 'has a benzene ring' (AK-RXN-01).
Benzaldehyde has zero $\alpha$-H; phenylacetaldehyde ($C_6H_5CH_2CHO$) has two.
No $\alpha$-H + conc. alkali $\to$ Cannizzaro; $\alpha$-H + dilute alkali $\to$ aldol (AK-RXN-02).
Ketones give no silver mirror and no red $Cu_2O$; Fehling's is aliphatic-aldehyde only (AK-RXN-03/04).
'Reduces' vs 'is reduced': an aldehyde reduces Tollens'; $NaBH_4$ reduces the carbonyl (AK-RXN-06).
Pro-tip checklist: $-CHO$? (Tollens/Fehling). $CH_3CO$–? (iodoform). $\alpha$-H? (aldol). No $\alpha$-H? (Cannizzaro).
For $\to CH_2$: acid-sensitive group $\to$ Wolff–Kishner; base-sensitive $\to$ Clemmensen (AK-RXN-05).

segments.text: Let us close with the slips that quietly cost marks in reactions questions, and the reflexes that prevent them.
First, and most common: count alpha-hydrogens from the alpha-carbon itself, never from a quick glance at whether there is a benzene ring.
Benzaldehyde has zero alpha-H, because the hydrogen on its C H O is not an alpha-H; but phenylacetaldehyde, phenyl-C H two-C H O, has two alpha-hydrogens on that C H two.
Second: no alpha-H with concentrated alkali gives Cannizzaro, while alpha-H present with dilute alkali gives aldol. An aldehyde with alpha-H never gives Cannizzaro because aldol is faster.
Third: never let a ketone pass Tollens' or Fehling's. Ketones give no silver mirror and no red cuprous oxide, and remember Fehling's works only for aliphatic aldehydes.

Fourth, a wording trap: an aldehyde reduces Tollens' reagent, meaning the aldehyde is oxidised and the silver is reduced, whereas sodium borohydride reduces the carbonyl. Read the direction of electron flow.

Here is the speed checklist for any which-test question: is there a C H O? think Tollens and Fehling. Is there a methyl carbonyl? think iodoform. Is there an alpha-H? think aldol. No alpha-H on an aldehyde? think Cannizzaro under concentrated alkali.
<whisper> And for reductions to C H two, the choice is purely medium compatibility: an acid-sensitive group pushes you to Wolff-Kishner, a base-sensitive group to Clemmensen.
चलिए उन slips के साथ बंद करते हैं जो reactions questions में चुपके से marks ले जाते हैं, और उन reflexes के साथ जो उन्हें रोकते हैं।
पहला, और सबसे common: alpha-hydrogens को alpha-carbon से गिनिए, कभी इस बात से नहीं कि benzene ring है या नहीं।
Benzaldehyde में zero alpha-H है, क्योंकि उसके C H O का hydrogen alpha-H नहीं है; पर phenylacetaldehyde, phenyl-C H two-C H O, में उस C H two पर दो alpha-hydrogens हैं।
दूसरा: कोई alpha-H नहीं with concentrated alkali Cannizzaro देता है, जबकि alpha-H present with dilute alkali aldol देता है। Alpha-H वाला aldehyde कभी Cannizzaro नहीं देता क्योंकि aldol तेज़ है।
तीसरा: एक ketone को कभी Tollens' या Fehling's pass मत करने दीजिए। Ketones कोई silver mirror और कोई red cuprous oxide नहीं देते, और याद रखिए Fehling's सिर्फ aliphatic aldehydes के लिए काम करता है।

चौथा, एक wording trap: एक aldehyde Tollens' reagent को reduce करता है, मतलब aldehyde oxidise होता है और silver reduce होता है, जबकि sodium borohydride carbonyl को reduce करता है। Electron flow की direction पढ़िए।

यह रही speed checklist किसी भी which-test question के लिए: C H O है? Tollens और Fehling सोचिए। Methyl carbonyl है? iodoform सोचिए। Alpha-H है? aldol सोचिए। Aldehyde पर कोई alpha-H नहीं? concentrated alkali में Cannizzaro सोचिए।
<whisper> और C H two तक reductions के लिए, choice पूरी तरह medium compatibility है: acid-sensitive group आपको Wolff-Kishner की तरफ ले जाता है, base-sensitive group Clemmensen की तरफ।

board_events.text: A carboxyl, $-COOH$, looks like a carbonyl fused to a hydroxyl — but it is not the sum of the two.
The hydroxyl oxygen keeps donating a lone pair into the carbonyl. Two things follow.
First: the carboxyl carbon becomes less electrophilic $\Rightarrow$ no simple nucleophilic addition (no HCN, no $NaHSO_3$).
Second: the O–H proton leaves easily, because the carboxylate spreads its charge over two equivalent oxygens.
A spread-out, stabilised anion is a happy anion — and a happy conjugate base means a willing acid.
So the whole sub-topic reduces to one question: how well can the conjugate base hold the charge?

segments.text: A carboxyl group looks like a carbonyl fused to a hydroxyl, but here is the surprise: it behaves like neither, because the two halves talk to each other through resonance.
The diagram shows the carboxylate ion, where the negative charge is not stuck in one place but shared across two oxygens.
So a carboxyl, minus C O O H, looks like a carbonyl with a hydroxyl attached, yet it is not simply the sum of the two.
The hydroxyl oxygen keeps donating one of its lone pairs into the neighbouring carbonyl, and two consequences follow.
First: the carboxyl carbon becomes less electrophilic, so it does not undergo the simple nucleophilic addition we saw for aldehydes, no hydrogen cyanide, no sodium bisulphite.
Second, and more importantly: the O-H proton leaves easily, because the resulting carboxylate spreads its negative charge equally over two equivalent oxygens.
A spread-out, stabilised anion is a happy anion, and a happy conjugate base means a willing acid.
So the whole sub-topic reduces to one question: how well can the conjugate base hold the negative charge?
एक carboxyl group एक carbonyl aur ek hydroxyl का mash-up दिखता है, पर asal में यह दोनों जैसा behave नहीं करता।
Diagram carboxylate ion दिखाता है, जहाँ negative charge एक जगह नहीं, दोनों oxygens पर बँटी है।
एक carboxyl, minus C O O H, carbonyl पर एक hydroxyl जुड़ा दिखता है, पर यह उन दोनों का sum नहीं है।
Hydroxyl oxygen लगातार अपना एक lone pair बगल वाले carbonyl में donate करता रहता है। इससे दो चीज़ें होती हैं।
पहली: carboxyl carbon कम electrophilic हो जाता है, इसलिए यहाँ simple nucleophilic addition नहीं होता, ना H C N, ना sodium bisulphite।
दूसरी: O-H proton आसानी से निकल जाता है, क्योंकि carboxylate अपनी charge दो equivalent oxygens पर फैला देता है।
एक फैली हुई, stabilised anion एक खुश anion है, और एक खुश conjugate base का मतलब एक willing acid।
तो पूरा sub-topic एक सवाल पर सिमट जाता है: conjugate base charge को कितनी अच्छी तरह पकड़ सकती है?

board_events.text: In a carboxylate, two strong equal runners (the two oxygens) share the charge — most comfortable.
A phenoxide passes the charge onto ring carbons — less electronegative, and the structures are not equivalent.
So a phenoxide is stabilised, but less effectively than a carboxylate.
An alkoxide has essentially one runner and no sharing at all — least comfortable, weakest acid.
Hence the hierarchy: carboxylic acid $>$ phenol $>$ alcohol.
Always argue from the anion's stability, never from the neutral acid molecule.

segments.text: Picture acidity like a relay team passing a hot potato, and the potato is the negative charge.
The diagram lines up three conjugate bases at three levels of comfort.
In a carboxylate, two strong and equally able runners, the two oxygens, share the charge, so it is the most comfortable.
A phenoxide instead passes the charge onto ring carbons, which are less electronegative, and its resonance structures are not even equivalent.
So a phenoxide is stabilised, but distinctly less effectively than a carboxylate.
An alkoxide has essentially one runner and no sharing at all, so it is the least comfortable and the weakest acid.
Hence the hierarchy you must know: carboxylic acid stronger than phenol stronger than alcohol.
And always argue from the stability of the anion, never from the neutral acid molecule.
Acidity को एक relay team की तरह सोचिए जो एक गरम आलू, यानी negative charge, pass कर रही है।

एक carboxylate में, दो strong बराबर runners, यानी दो oxygens, charge को share करते हैं, सबसे comfortable।
एक phenoxide charge को ring carbons पर pass करता है, जो कम electronegative हैं, और structures equivalent भी नहीं हैं।
तो एक phenoxide stabilised तो होता है, पर carboxylate से कम effectively।
एक alkoxide में बस एक runner है और कोई sharing नहीं, सबसे कम comfortable, सबसे weak acid।
इसलिए hierarchy: carboxylic acid greater than phenol greater than alcohol।
हमेशा anion की stability से argue कीजिए, कभी neutral acid molecule से नहीं।

board_events.text: Distance matters: a halogen on the $\alpha$-carbon strengthens the acid far more than the same halogen further down.
Electron-donating groups (alkyl, $-OCH_3$) pile charge onto the anion and weaken the acid.

segments.text: Now how substituents shift acidity: electron pull raises it, while distance and electron donation lower it.
The diagram shows both the pull series and the aromatic examples.
An electron-withdrawing group, a minus-I group, pulls charge away from the carboxylate, spreading it and stabilising the anion.
The order of increasing pull runs: phenyl, then iodine, bromine, chlorine, fluorine, then the cyano group, the nitro group, and the strongest, the trifluoromethyl group.
Distance matters a lot: a halogen on the alpha-carbon strengthens the acid far more than the same halogen placed further down the chain.
Electron-donating groups, such as alkyl chains or a methoxy group, pile charge onto the anion and weaken the acid.

On a benzene ring the same logic applies: an electron-withdrawing group raises acidity, so four-nitrobenzoic acid is stronger, while an electron-donating group lowers it, so four-methoxybenzoic acid is weaker than benzoic.
One twist to remember: a directly attached phenyl or vinyl group actually raises acidity, because the s p two carbon it bonds to is more electronegative than an s p three alkyl carbon.
एक electron-withdrawing group, यानी minus I, charge को खींचकर anion को stabilise करता है, और यही acidity का इंजन है।
Diagram यह pull series aur aromatic examples दोनों दिखाता है।
पहले aliphatic pull: एक minus I group जितना strong होगा, anion उतना stable, acid उतना strong।
Order बढ़ते pull के साथ: phenyl, फिर I, Br, Cl, F, C N, N O two, और सबसे ऊपर C F three।
Distance मायने रखती है: alpha-carbon पर एक halogen acid को कहीं ज़्यादा strong बनाता है उसी halogen से जो chain में आगे हो।
Electron-donating groups, जैसे alkyl या minus O C H three, charge को anion पर और लाद कर acid को weak करते हैं।
Ring पर: E W G acidity बढ़ाता है, four-nitrobenzoic strongest; E D G घटाता है, four-methoxybenzoic weakest, बीच में benzoic।
एक twist: सीधे जुड़ा phenyl या vinyl acidity बढ़ाता है, क्योंकि जिस s p two carbon से bond बनता है वह ज़्यादा electronegative है।

segments.text: For preparation, the skill is matching the starting material to the right road.
The diagram shows six roads that all end at the carboxyl group.
Route one: oxidise a primary alcohol or an aldehyde, using a strong oxidant, or a mild one if you are starting from the aldehyde.
Route two: vigorously oxidise an alkylbenzene side chain, and the whole chain becomes a carboxyl group, though a tertiary benzylic carbon with no benzylic hydrogen resists.
Route three: hydrolyse a nitrile or an amide, with either acid or base.
Route four: a Grignard reagent plus carbon dioxide, that is dry ice, then aqueous acid; this route climbs the chain by one carbon.
Route five: hydrolyse an acyl halide or an anhydride; and route six: hydrolyse an ester, either directly with acid or with base and then acidify.
So if you need exactly one more carbon than your alkyl halide, the Grignard-plus-carbon-dioxide route, or going via the nitrile, is the signature move.
Preparation में starting material को road से match करना है।
Diagram छह roads दिखाता है जो सब minus C O O H पर खत्म होते हैं।
एक: एक primary alcohol या एक aldehyde को oxidise कीजिए, strong oxidant से, या aldehyde के लिए mild से।
दो: एक alkylbenzene side chain को vigorously oxidise कीजिए, पूरी chain minus C O O H बन जाती है, par एक tertiary benzylic carbon resist करता है।
तीन: एक nitrile या amide को acid या base से hydrolyse कीजिए।
चार: Grignard plus carbon dioxide, यानी dry ice, फिर aqueous acid, यह route chain को एक carbon से बढ़ाता है।
पाँच: एक acyl halide या anhydride को hydrolyse कीजिए; छह: एक ester को hydrolyse कीजिए, acidic, या basic फिर acidify।
अपने alkyl halide से एक carbon ज़्यादा चाहिए? Grignard plus carbon dioxide, या nitrile के रास्ते, इसका signature है।

board_events.text: With an active metal, a carboxylic acid gives a salt and releases hydrogen gas.
With NaOH it simply gives the salt and water.
Uniquely, even the weak bases $Na_2CO_3$ and $NaHCO_3$ are deprotonated, releasing $CO_2$.
That last reaction is the standard lab detection test for a $-COOH$ group.
It is also the clean way to tell an acid from a phenol: the acid fizzes, the phenol does not.
Every one of these is the acidic O–H being handed off — the theme of the whole first half.

segments.text: The first family of reactions breaks the O-H bond, the acidic reactions.
The diagram lays out metals, alkali, and the special carbonate-or-bicarbonate tell.
With an active metal, a carboxylic acid gives a salt and releases hydrogen gas.
With sodium hydroxide it simply gives the salt and water.
Uniquely, even the weak bases sodium carbonate and sodium bicarbonate are strong enough to deprotonate it, releasing carbon dioxide.
That last reaction is the standard laboratory detection test for a carboxyl group.
It is also the clean way to tell an acid from a phenol: the acid fizzes off carbon dioxide, the phenol does not.
Every one of these is really the acidic O-H being handed off, the unifying theme of the first half of the sub-topic.
पहली category: O-H bond टूटना, यानी acidic reactions।
Diagram metals, alkali, aur carbonate ya bicarbonate का tell दिखाता है।
एक active metal के साथ, एक carboxylic acid एक salt देता है और hydrogen gas छोड़ता है।
N a O H के साथ यह बस salt और water देता है।
खास बात, weak bases sodium carbonate aur sodium bicarbonate भी deprotonate हो जाते हैं, carbon dioxide छोड़ते हुए।
वही आखिरी reaction एक minus C O O H group का standard lab detection test है।
यही एक acid को phenol से अलग करने का clean तरीका भी है: acid fizz करता है, phenol नहीं।
इनमें से हर एक acidic O-H का hand-off है, पहले half का पूरा theme।
