board_events.text: The carboxyl carbon is too weakly electrophilic for addition, so it does substitution: the –OH is turned into a leaving group.
Esterification (alcohol, conc. $H_2SO_4$): protonate C=O, alcohol adds, shift a proton so $-OH$ becomes $-OH_2^+$, water leaves.
Every step is reversible, so it is an equilibrium — drive it with excess alcohol or by removing water.
$SOCl_2$ swaps $-OH$ for $-Cl$ (acyl chloride); its by-products $SO_2$ and HCl are gases, so the product is clean.
Heating with $H_2SO_4$ or $P_2O_5$ gives an anhydride; $NH_3$ then heat gives an amide.
These are all C–OH swaps — a family distinct from the O–H acidity reactions.

segments.text: The second family breaks the carbon-to-hydroxyl bond, and its centrepiece is esterification.
The diagram frames esterification as a reversible nucleophilic acyl substitution.
The carboxyl carbon is too weakly electrophilic for simple addition, so instead it does substitution: the hydroxyl is converted into a leaving group.
In esterification, with an alcohol and concentrated sulphuric acid: protonate the carbonyl, the alcohol adds, a proton shifts so the hydroxyl becomes a water leaving group, and water departs.
Every step is reversible, so the whole thing is an equilibrium; drive it forward with excess alcohol or by removing water as it forms.
Thionyl chloride swaps the hydroxyl for a chlorine, giving an acyl chloride; its by-products, sulphur dioxide and hydrogen chloride, are gases that escape, leaving a clean product.
Heating with sulphuric acid or phosphorus pentoxide gives an anhydride, and ammonia followed by heat gives an amide.
These are all carbon-to-hydroxyl swaps, a family quite distinct from the O-H acidity reactions.
दूसरी category: C-OH bond टूटना, और इसका दिल esterification है।
Diagram esterification को एक reversible acyl substitution की तरह दिखाता है।
Carboxyl carbon addition के लिए बहुत weakly electrophilic है, इसलिए यह substitution करता है: minus O H को एक leaving group में बदल दिया जाता है।
Esterification, alcohol aur concentrated sulphuric acid के साथ: C=O को protonate कीजिए, alcohol add होता है, एक proton shift होता है ताकि minus O H, minus O H two plus बन जाए, water निकल जाता है।
हर step reversible है, इसलिए यह एक equilibrium है, इसे excess alcohol से या water हटा कर आगे बढ़ाइए।
Thionyl chloride, minus O H को minus C l से बदल देता है, यानी acyl chloride; इसके by-products sulphur dioxide aur H C l gases हैं, तो product clean रहता है।
Sulphuric acid या phosphorus pentoxide के साथ heat करने पर anhydride मिलता है; ammonia फिर heat amide देता है।
ये सब C-OH swaps हैं, O-H acidity reactions से अलग एक family।

board_events.text: Reduction: $LiAlH_4$ or diborane takes $-COOH$ to a $1^\circ$ alcohol; $NaBH_4$ is too weak to touch it.
Diborane spares esters, nitro and halo groups — the chemoselective choice when those must survive.
Decarboxylation: heat the sodium salt with sodalime to expel $CO_2$, giving a hydrocarbon with one fewer carbon.
Kolbe electrolysis instead couples two alkyl fragments from the carboxylate salt.
HVZ: an acid with an $\alpha$-H is halogenated at the $\alpha$-carbon by $Cl_2/Br_2$ and a little red phosphorus.
Aromatic ring: $-COOH$ is deactivating and meta-directing, and the ring will not do Friedel–Crafts.

segments.text: The third family gathers three more transformations, plus one wonderfully selective reagent.
The diagram groups reduction, decarboxylation, and the aromatic ring behaviour.
Reduction: lithium aluminium hydride or diborane takes the carboxyl all the way to a primary alcohol, while sodium borohydride is simply too weak to touch it.
Diborane also spares esters, nitro and halo groups, which makes it the chemoselective choice when those groups must survive.
Decarboxylation: heat the sodium salt with sodalime to expel carbon dioxide, giving a hydrocarbon with one fewer carbon.
Kolbe electrolysis does something different: it couples two alkyl fragments from the carboxylate salt.
The H V Z reaction: an acid bearing an alpha-hydrogen is halogenated at the alpha-carbon by chlorine or bromine with a little red phosphorus.
And on an aromatic ring, the carboxyl group is deactivating and meta-directing, and the ring will not undergo Friedel-Crafts.
तीसरी category: तीन और reactions, aur एक chemoselective reagent।
Diagram reduction, decarboxylation aur aromatic ring दिखाता है।
Reduction: lithium aluminium hydride या diborane minus C O O H को एक primary alcohol तक ले जाते हैं; sodium borohydride इसे छूने के लिए बहुत weak है।

board_events.text: Reason about the conjugate base: pull raises acidity, alkyl donation lowers it.
Propanoic acid: an extra $+I$ alkyl carbon destabilises the anion $\Rightarrow$ weakest.
Acetic acid: one methyl, less $+I$ than propanoic's ethyl $\Rightarrow$ next.
Chloroacetic: Cl is $-I$, stabilises the anion $\Rightarrow$ stronger.
State the principle for the mark: EWG stabilise the carboxylate and strengthen the acid.

segments.text: This C B S E-style question asks you to rank four acids, and every step flows from the conjugate base.
The diagram orders them by the electron pull on the alpha-carbon.
Reason about the conjugate base: electron pull raises acidity, while alkyl donation lowers it.
Propanoic acid has an extra plus-I alkyl carbon that destabilises the anion, so it is the weakest.
Acetic acid has one methyl, a smaller plus-I push than propanoic's ethyl, so it comes next.
Chloroacetic acid carries a chlorine, which is minus-I and stabilises the anion, so it is stronger.
So the order runs: propanoic, then acetic, then chloroacetic, then the strongest, fluoroacetic, since fluorine is the most electronegative halogen.
State the principle for the reasoning mark: electron-withdrawing groups stabilise the carboxylate and strengthen the acid.
यह C B S E-style सवाल chaar acids को rank करवाता है, aur jawaab conjugate base से आता है।
Diagram order को alpha-carbon पर electron pull से दिखाता है।
Conjugate base के बारे में सोचिए: pull acidity बढ़ाता है, alkyl donation उसे घटाता है।
Propanoic acid: एक extra plus I alkyl carbon anion को destabilise करता है, इसलिए सबसे weak।
Acetic acid: एक methyl, propanoic के ethyl से कम plus I, इसलिए अगला।
Chloroacetic: C l minus I है, anion को stabilise करता है, इसलिए ज़्यादा strong।
तो order: propanoic, फिर acetic, फिर chloroacetic, फिर सबसे strong fluoroacetic।
Mark के लिए principle likhiye: E W G carboxylate को stabilise करके acid को strong बनाते हैं।

segments.text: This N E E T speed trap asks you to tell benzoic acid from phenol with a single reagent.
The diagram shows that only bicarbonate cleanly separates them.
Here is the trap: both are acidic and both react with sodium hydroxide, so sodium hydroxide cannot distinguish them.
The key is that carboxylic acids are strong enough to react with the weak base sodium bicarbonate, whereas phenols are not.

This bicarbonate test is the standard one-step discriminator.

segments.text: This J E E Main question converts two starting materials, each into its appropriate acid.
The diagram contrasts the climb-a-carbon route with side-chain oxidation.
Bromoethane goes to propanoic acid by ascending the chain: form the Grignard, then add carbon dioxide.
In symbols: bromoethane with magnesium gives the Grignard reagent, then carbon dioxide and aqueous acid deliver propanoic acid.

यह J E E Main सवाल दो starting materials को unke acids में बदलवाता है।

Bromoethane, propanoic acid में बदलता है chain को बढ़ाकर, Grignard फिर carbon dioxide से।

segments.text: This J E E Advanced question first asks a chemoselective reduction, then a positional acidity comparison.
The diagram casts diborane as the Goldilocks reagent, neither too strong nor too weak.
The molecule contains both a carboxyl group and an ester, and you must reduce only the acid to a primary alcohol.
Lithium aluminium hydride is too strong, because it also reduces the ester; sodium borohydride is too weak, because it ignores the acid entirely.
Diborane is just right: it reduces the carboxyl to a primary alcohol but leaves esters, nitro and halo groups untouched.
For the positional part: two-chlorobutanoic acid is a stronger acid than four-chlorobutanoic acid.
The inductive effect falls steeply with distance, so a chlorine on the alpha-carbon stabilises the carboxylate far more than one three carbons away.
The examiner is testing two precise ideas at once: reagent chemoselectivity and the distance-dependence of the minus-I effect.
यह J E E Advanced सवाल acid को reduce करवाता है par ester बचाकर, फिर दो acids को rank करवाता है।

एक molecule में minus C O O H aur एक ester दोनों हैं; सिर्फ acid को एक primary alcohol में reduce कीजिए।
Lithium aluminium hydride बहुत strong है, ester को भी reduce करता है; sodium borohydride बहुत weak है, acid को ignore करता है।
Diborane, B two H six, minus C O O H को primary alcohol में reduce करता है par esters, nitro aur halo को छोड़ देता है।
Positional acidity: two-chlorobutanoic acid, four-chlorobutanoic acid से ज़्यादा strong है।
Induction distance के साथ तेज़ी से गिरती है: alpha-carbon पर C l carboxylate को कहीं ज़्यादा stabilise करता है।
Examiner एक साथ दो ideas target करता है: reagent chemoselectivity aur minus I की distance-dependence।

board_events.text: Where acid questions quietly go wrong
Ignoring inductive distance: an $\alpha$-halogen beats the same halogen further along (CA-ACID-01).
Reasoning from the acid, not the conjugate base — always argue from carboxylate stability (CA-ACID-02).
$NaBH_4$ does NOT reduce $-COOH$; use $LiAlH_4$ or diborane, and diborane spares esters (CA-RED-01).
Using NaOH to separate an acid from a phenol — only $NaHCO_3$ distinguishes them (CA-TEST-01).
Expecting nucleophilic addition: resonance lowers the carboxyl carbon; it does acyl substitution (CA-STR-01).
Pro-tip: for acidity, run a conjugate-base audit — count EWG vs EDG, then apply a distance penalty ($\alpha$ beats $\beta$).
For 'distinguish' involving an acid, the bicarbonate $CO_2$ test is almost always the intended answer.

segments.text: Let us close with the slips that quietly cost marks in carboxylic-acid questions.
First, ignoring inductive distance: an alpha-halogen strengthens the acid far more than the same halogen further along the chain.
Second, reasoning from the acid instead of the conjugate base; always argue from carboxylate stability after the proton has left.
Third, do not think sodium borohydride reduces a carboxyl group; it does not, so use lithium aluminium hydride or diborane, and remember diborane spares esters.
Fourth, do not use sodium hydroxide to separate an acid from a phenol, because both react with it; only sodium bicarbonate distinguishes them.
Fifth, do not expect nucleophilic addition; resonance lowers the carboxyl carbon's electrophilicity, so it reacts by acyl substitution instead.
The pro-tip: for any acidity ranking, run a conjugate-base audit, count electron-withdrawing versus electron-donating groups, then apply a distance penalty, since alpha beats beta beats gamma.
And for any distinguish question involving an acid, the bicarbonate carbon-dioxide test is almost always the intended one-step answer.
चलिए उन slips के साथ बंद करते हैं जो acid questions में चुपके से marks ले जाते हैं।
Inductive distance को ignore करना: एक alpha-halogen उसी halogen को हराता है जो chain में आगे हो।
Acid से reason करना, conjugate base से नहीं, हमेशा carboxylate stability से argue कीजिए।
Sodium borohydride minus C O O H को reduce नहीं करता; lithium aluminium hydride या diborane use कीजिए, aur diborane esters को छोड़ देता है।
एक acid को phenol से अलग करने के लिए N a O H use करना, सिर्फ sodium bicarbonate इन्हें distinguish करता है।
Nucleophilic addition की उम्मीद करना: resonance carboxyl carbon को कम electrophilic करता है; यह acyl substitution करता है।
Pro-tip: acidity के लिए एक conjugate-base audit चलाइए, E W G बनाम E D G गिनिए, फिर distance penalty लगाइए, alpha beta को हराता है।
किसी acid वाले distinguish सवाल के लिए, bicarbonate carbon dioxide test लगभग हमेशा intended answer होता है।

board_events.text: Boiling means everyone lets go and runs off as individuals — how hard depends on how tightly they hold hands.

segments.text: Every physical property of these molecules traces back to one idea: how strongly they cling to one another and to water.
The diagram is a boiling-point ladder with five rungs of increasing attraction.
Boiling means every molecule must let go and run off as an individual into the gas phase, and how hard that is depends on how tightly they are holding hands.
A pure hydrocarbon is like strangers brushing past: only weak van der Waals dispersion, the faintest grip, so it boils low.
Aldehydes and ketones carry a permanent dipole, the polar carbon-oxygen bond, so they align like weak magnets, a firmer dipole-dipole handshake.
Alcohols go further with a proper O-H hydrogen bond, and carboxylic acids are the champions, clasping into a dimer held by two hydrogen bonds at once.
So the ladder reads: hydrocarbon, then ether, then aldehyde or ketone, then alcohol, then carboxylic acid at the top.
A memory aid ties it together: He Eats Apples Like Candy, for Hydrocarbon, Ether, Aldehyde-ketone, aLcohol, Carboxylic acid.
इन molecules की हर physical property एक idea पर टिकी है: ये एक दूसरे से aur water से कितनी मज़बूती से चिपकती हैं।
Diagram एक boiling-point ladder है जिसमें बढ़ती attraction के पाँच rungs हैं।
Boiling का मतलब हर molecule को छोड़कर एक individual की तरह gas phase में भागना होता है, aur यह कितना मुश्किल है वह इस पर depend करता है कि वे कितनी कसकर हाथ पकड़े हैं।
एक pure hydrocarbon अजनबियों की तरह है जो बगल से गुज़र जाते हैं: सिर्फ weak van der Waals dispersion, सबसे हल्की पकड़, तो यह low boil करता है।
Aldehydes aur ketones एक permanent dipole रखते हैं, polar carbon-oxygen bond, तो वे weak magnets की तरह align होते हैं, एक मज़बूत dipole-dipole handshake।
Alcohols एक proper O-H hydrogen bond के साथ और आगे जाते हैं, aur carboxylic acids champions हैं, एक dimer में clasp करते हैं जो एक साथ दो hydrogen bonds से बँधा है।
तो ladder इस तरह पढ़ी जाती है: hydrocarbon, फिर ether, फिर aldehyde या ketone, फिर alcohol, फिर सबसे ऊपर carboxylic acid।
एक memory aid इसे जोड़ता है: He Eats Apples Like Candy, यानी Hydrocarbon, Ether, Aldehyde-ketone, aLcohol, Carboxylic acid।

segments.text: Here are the numbers behind that ladder.
The diagram tabulates boiling points at comparable molecular mass, so the force is what decides.
The forces, weakest to strongest, run: van der Waals dispersion, then dipole-dipole, then hydrogen bond, then the double-hydrogen-bonded dimer.

Aldehydes and ketones boil above hydrocarbons and ethers because of that dipole, but below alcohols of similar mass, because they have no O-H hydrogen-bond donor.

board_events.text: Step 1: identify the strongest force each molecule can form — the one with the stronger force boils higher.
Step 2: break ties with mass (heavier boils higher) and shape (less branched boils higher).
A ketone edges above its isomeric aldehyde: propanal $322$ K vs acetone $329$ K.

segments.text: To rank boiling points reliably, use two steps.
The diagram captures the subtle within-family effects.
Step one: identify the strongest intermolecular force each molecule can form; the one with the stronger force boils higher.
Step two: break ties with mass, the heavier boils higher, and with shape, the less branched boils higher because it has more surface contact.
Watch this subtlety: a ketone edges just above its isomeric aldehyde, propanal at three hundred twenty-two kelvin versus acetone at three hundred twenty-nine.
The reason is that the ketone's carbonyl sits in the middle of the chain, where the molecular dipole is expressed a little better.
From the other side, an ether's two carbon-oxygen dipoles are oriented so as to partly cancel, so ethers sit only just above hydrocarbons.
And crucially, no carbonyl can match an alcohol of equal mass, because the decisive factor is the presence of an O-H donor, not the mere existence of an oxygen atom.
Boiling points को reliably rank करने के लिए दो steps use कीजिए।
Diagram इन subtle within-family effects को पकड़ता है।
Step एक: पहचानिए कि हर molecule कौन सी strongest intermolecular force बना सकता है; जिसकी force strong, वह higher boil करता है।
Step दो: ties को mass से तोड़िए, heavier higher boil करता है, aur shape से, less branched higher boil करता है क्योंकि उसका surface contact ज़्यादा है।
यह subtlety देखिए: एक ketone अपने isomeric aldehyde से थोड़ा ऊपर निकलता है, propanal three hundred twenty-two kelvin par acetone three hundred twenty-nine।
वजह यह है कि ketone का carbonyl chain के बीच में बैठता है, जहाँ molecular dipole थोड़ा बेहतर express होता है।
दूसरी तरफ, एक ether के दो carbon-oxygen dipoles इस तरह oriented हैं कि वे partly cancel कर देते हैं, तो ethers hydrocarbons से बस थोड़ा ऊपर बैठते हैं।
aur खास बात, कोई carbonyl समान mass के alcohol की बराबरी नहीं कर सकता, क्योंकि decisive factor एक O-H donor का होना है, सिर्फ एक oxygen atom का होना नहीं।

segments.text: Water solubility follows a parallel logic, but asks a different question: can the molecule hold hands with water?
The diagram frames it as a tug-of-war between a polar head and a greasy tail.
The small members, methanal, ethanal, propanone and the small acids, hydrogen-bond with water through their oxygen atoms and dissolve freely.
But every one of these molecules also drags a greasy hydrocarbon tail that water rejects.
As that tail grows, the water-friendly head is outvoted by the water-hating tail, and solubility falls off until the higher members are essentially insoluble.
Physical state follows the very same forces: methanal is a gas, ethanal a low-boiling volatile liquid, and the higher members, with aromatic acids, are solids.
Odour is the most human property: the smaller aldehydes are sharp and pungent, while larger molecules mellow into something fragrant, which is why perfumery is full of medium-sized carbonyls.
And regardless of water solubility, all of these compounds dissolve readily in less-polar organic solvents like benzene, ether and chloroform.
Water solubility एक parallel logic follow करती है, par एक अलग सवाल पूछती है: क्या molecule water के साथ हाथ पकड़ सकता है?
Diagram इसे एक polar head aur एक greasy tail के बीच tug-of-war की तरह दिखाता है।
Small members, methanal, ethanal, propanone aur small acids, अपने oxygen atoms से water के साथ hydrogen-bond करते हैं aur freely घुल जाते हैं।
par इनमें से हर molecule एक greasy hydrocarbon tail भी घसीटता है जिसे water reject करता है।
जैसे वह tail बढ़ती है, water-friendly head, water-hating tail से हार जाता है, aur solubility गिरती जाती है जब तक higher members लगभग insoluble न हो जाएँ।
Physical state उन्हीं forces को follow करती है: methanal एक gas है, ethanal एक low-boiling volatile liquid, aur higher members, aromatic acids के साथ, solids हैं।
Odour सबसे human property है: छोटे aldehydes sharp aur pungent होते हैं, जबकि बड़े molecules fragrant में mellow हो जाते हैं, इसीलिए perfumery medium-sized carbonyls से भरी है।
aur water solubility चाहे जो हो, ये सब compounds कम-polar organic solvents जैसे benzene, ether aur chloroform में आसानी से घुल जाते हैं।

segments.text: Uses are not arbitrary; they follow directly from the chemistry.
The diagram splits the aldehyde-ketone uses from the acid uses.
Methanal, sold as formalin, a forty percent aqueous solution, preserves biological specimens; it also builds bakelite and urea-formaldehyde resins.
Acetaldehyde is the industrial precursor to acetic acid; benzaldehyde serves perfumery and dyes; acetone and methyl ethyl ketone are common solvents.
Among acids, formic acid works in leather and textiles; acetic acid is table vinegar; and adipic acid, that is hexanedioic acid, makes nylon-six-six.
Sodium benzoate is a food preservative, and fatty acids, with their greasy tail and salt-forming head, are exactly what a soap needs.
Turning to the ring: an attached formyl, acyl or carboxyl group is electron-withdrawing in every case.
So all of them are deactivating and meta-directing: electrophilic substitution is slower than on benzene, and the incoming group prefers the meta position.
Uses arbitrary नहीं हैं; वे सीधे chemistry से निकलते हैं।
Diagram aldehyde-ketone uses को acid uses से अलग करता है।
Methanal, formalin के रूप में बिकता है, एक forty percent aqueous solution, biological specimens को preserve करता है; यह bakelite aur urea-formaldehyde resins भी बनाता है।
Acetaldehyde acetic acid का industrial precursor है; benzaldehyde perfumery aur dyes में काम आता है; acetone aur methyl ethyl ketone common solvents हैं।
Acids में, formic acid leather aur textiles में काम करता है; acetic acid table vinegar है; aur adipic acid, यानी hexanedioic acid, nylon-six-six बनाता है।
Sodium benzoate एक food preservative है, aur fatty acids, अपनी greasy tail aur salt-forming head के साथ, बिलकुल वही हैं जो एक soap को चाहिए।
Ring की तरफ आएँ: एक जुड़ा formyl, acyl या carboxyl group हर case में electron-withdrawing है।
तो ये सब deactivating aur meta-directing हैं: electrophilic substitution benzene से धीमी है, aur आने वाला group meta position पसंद करता है।

segments.text: This last teaching section is the glue: these physical properties explain choices made elsewhere in the chapter.
The diagram draws four cross-links back through the earlier sub-topics.
First, bisulphite purification from sub-topic two: the addition compound is deliberately water-soluble and crystalline, so a chemist can pull out a pure aldehyde as a solid and then regenerate it.
Second, why formalin is aqueous: methanal is a gas and very water-soluble, so it is sold as the convenient forty percent aqueous solution rather than the awkward gas.

Third, the dimer from sub-topic three: the same double hydrogen bonding that gives carboxylic acids their record boiling points also reflects the polarised carboxyl group whose anion stability makes them so acidic.
Fourth, solubility and detection: the brisk water solubility of small acids is exactly what makes the sodium bicarbonate carbon-dioxide test a clean aqueous-phase identification.
So if you remember that an aldehyde has a polar carbon-oxygen bond but no O-H, you can derive its boiling-point rank and its water solubility on the spot.
Seeing these threads means a student reconstructs facts rather than recalling a rote-learned table, which is what real mastery feels like.
यह आखिरी teaching section glue है: ये physical properties chapter में कहीं और लिए गए choices को explain करती हैं।

चौथा, solubility aur detection: small acids की तेज़ water solubility ही sodium bicarbonate carbon-dioxide test को एक clean aqueous-phase identification बनाती है।
तो अगर आपको याद है कि एक aldehyde में polar carbon-oxygen bond है par O-H नहीं, तो आप इसका boiling-point rank aur water solubility मौके पर derive कर सकते हैं।

segments.text: This C B S E-style question asks you to rank four four-carbon molecules by boiling point.
The diagram shows that with equal masses, the force alone decides.
Since all four have similar molecular mass, the strongest intermolecular force each can form decides the order.
Butane has only van der Waals dispersion, so it is the lowest.
Butanal has a polar carbonyl, giving dipole-dipole attraction, which is stronger than butane's dispersion.
Butan-one-ol has an O-H hydrogen bond, stronger still than dipole-dipole.
So the order runs: butane, then butanal, then butan-one-ol, then butanoic acid, which forms the double-hydrogen-bonded dimer.
State the rule for the reasoning mark: boiling point rises with the strength of intermolecular attraction.
यह C B S E-style सवाल chaar four-carbon molecules को boiling point से rank करवाता है।
Diagram दिखाता है कि equal masses के साथ, सिर्फ force decide करती है।
चूँकि chaaron की molecular mass समान है, हर एक जो strongest intermolecular force बना सकता है वही order decide करती है।
Butane में सिर्फ van der Waals dispersion है, तो यह सबसे नीचे है।
Butanal में एक polar carbonyl है, जो dipole-dipole attraction देता है, जो butane के dispersion से strong है।
Butan-one-ol में एक O-H hydrogen bond है, dipole-dipole से भी strong।
तो order इस तरह है: butane, फिर butanal, फिर butan-one-ol, फिर butanoic acid, जो double-hydrogen-bonded dimer बनाता है।
Reasoning mark के लिए rule likhiye: boiling point intermolecular attraction की strength के साथ बढ़ता है।

board_events.text: Trap: seeing 'acid' and assuming it must be most soluble — decanoic acid drags a ten-carbon tail.

segments.text: This NEET speed trap asks which of four compounds is most soluble in water.
The diagram makes the rule visual: strongest head, shortest tail wins.
Here is the trap: students see the word acid and assume it must be most soluble, because acids hydrogen-bond strongly, forgetting the tail.
The real rule is best solubility equals the strongest polar head and the shortest tail.
Propanone is a tiny three-carbon ketone, and it is miscible with water in all proportions.
Decanoic acid, by contrast, drags a ten-carbon hydrophobic tail that makes it essentially insoluble, despite its acid head.
So the answer is propanone, that is acetone.
Once the head can hydrogen-bond, rank purely by tail length; the shortest tail wins.
यह N E E T speed trap पूछता है कि chaar compounds में से कौन सा water में सबसे ज़्यादा soluble है।
Diagram rule को visual बनाता है: strongest head, shortest tail जीतता है।
Trap यह है: students acid शब्द देखकर मान लेते हैं कि वही सबसे soluble होगा, क्योंकि acids strong hydrogen-bond करते हैं, tail भूल जाते हैं।
असली rule यह है कि best solubility का मतलब strongest polar head aur shortest tail।
Propanone एक tiny three-carbon ketone है, aur यह water के साथ हर proportion में miscible है।
Decanoic acid, इसके उलट, एक ten-carbon hydrophobic tail घसीटता है जो इसे अपने acid head के बावजूद लगभग insoluble बना देता है।
तो answer है propanone, यानी acetone।
एक बार head hydrogen-bond कर सके, तो सिर्फ tail length से rank कीजिए; shortest tail जीतती है।

board_events.text: Both molecules hydrogen-bond, so mass alone cannot explain the gap.
Ethanoic acid forms a cyclic dimer held by two hydrogen bonds at once — an effective unit of about double the mass.
Propan-1-ol forms only a chain of single hydrogen bonds, individually easier to break.
More hydrogen bonds per association event means more energy to vaporise, hence the higher boiling point.

The Advanced insight: the anomaly is a dimerisation effect, not a per-molecule hydrogen-bond effect.

segments.text: This J E E Advanced question compares two molecules of nearly identical mass that nonetheless boil quite differently.
The diagram sets ethanoic acid at three hundred ninety-one kelvin against propan-one-ol at three hundred seventy.
Both molecules hydrogen-bond, so molecular mass alone cannot explain the twenty-one kelvin gap.
The decisive difference is that ethanoic acid forms a cyclic dimer held together by two hydrogen bonds at once, so the species you must separate is effectively a unit of about double the molar mass.
Propan-one-ol, by contrast, forms only a chain of single hydrogen bonds, which are individually easier to disrupt.
More hydrogen bonds broken per association event means more energy needed to vaporise, and hence the higher boiling point.
For the gas-phase prediction: the dimer is most favoured in the vapour, where there is no competing solvent to break it, so the acid persists as dimers and the gap from the alcohol widens.
The Advanced-level insight is that this anomaly is a dimerisation effect, not a simple per-molecule hydrogen-bond-strength effect.
यह J E E Advanced सवाल लगभग समान mass के दो molecules की तुलना करता है जो फिर भी काफ़ी अलग boil करते हैं।
Diagram ethanoic acid को three hundred ninety-one kelvin par propan-one-ol को three hundred seventy पर रखता है।
दोनों molecules hydrogen-bond करते हैं, तो सिर्फ molecular mass इस twenty-one kelvin के gap को explain नहीं कर सकती।
Decisive फर्क यह है कि ethanoic acid एक cyclic dimer बनाता है जो एक साथ दो hydrogen bonds से बँधा है, तो जिस species को अलग करना है वह असल में लगभग double molar mass की एक unit है।
Propan-one-ol, इसके उलट, सिर्फ single hydrogen bonds की एक chain बनाता है, जो अलग-अलग तोड़ना आसान है।
हर association event में ज़्यादा hydrogen bonds टूटने का मतलब vaporise करने के लिए ज़्यादा energy, aur इसलिए higher boiling point।
Gas-phase prediction के लिए: dimer vapour में सबसे favoured है, जहाँ इसे तोड़ने के लिए कोई competing solvent नहीं, तो acid dimers के रूप में बना रहता है aur alcohol से gap बढ़ जाता है।
Advanced-level insight यह है कि यह anomaly एक dimerisation effect है, ना कि एक simple per-molecule hydrogen-bond-strength effect।

board_events.text: Where property questions quietly go wrong
Comparing boiling points without equalising mass — a heavy hydrocarbon can out-boil a light acid (PP-BP-01).
Thinking aldehydes/ketones hydrogen-bond like alcohols — they have dipole–dipole but no O–H donor (PP-BP-02).
Forgetting the hydrophobic tail: a strong polar head does not guarantee solubility (decanoic acid) (PP-SOL-01).
Calling the aromatic carbonyl ring ortho/para-directing — EWG carbonyls are deactivating, meta-directing (PP-SUB-01).
Pro-tip: run a 5-second force audit (dispersion / dipole / H-bond / dimer), order by that, then break ties with mass and branching.
For uses, anchor on the four classics: formalin, vinegar, nylon-6,6, sodium benzoate (USE-01).
For solubility rankings, additionally eyeball the tail length once the head can hydrogen-bond.

segments.text: Let us close the sub-topic with the slips that quietly cost marks on property questions.
First, comparing boiling points without equalising mass: the ladder assumes comparable mass, and a heavy hydrocarbon can out-boil a light acid.
Second, thinking aldehydes and ketones hydrogen-bond like alcohols: they have dipole-dipole attraction but no O-H donor, so they boil below alcohols of similar mass.
Third, forgetting the hydrophobic tail: a strong polar head does not guarantee water solubility if the chain is long, as decanoic acid shows.
Fourth, calling the aromatic carbonyl ring ortho or para-directing: electron-withdrawing carbonyl groups are deactivating and meta-directing.
The pro-tip: run a five-second force audit, label each molecule dispersion, dipole, hydrogen-bond or dimer, order by that first, then break ties with mass and branching.
For uses questions, anchor on the four classics examiners love: formalin for preserving, vinegar for acetic acid, nylon-six-six for adipic acid, and sodium benzoate as a preservative.
And for any solubility ranking, additionally eyeball the tail length once you have confirmed the head can hydrogen-bond.
चलिए sub-topic को उन slips के साथ बंद करते हैं जो property questions पर चुपके से marks ले जाते हैं।
पहला, boiling points को mass बराबर किए बिना compare करना: ladder comparable mass मानती है, aur एक heavy hydrocarbon एक light acid से ऊपर boil कर सकता है।
दूसरा, यह सोचना कि aldehydes aur ketones alcohols की तरह hydrogen-bond करते हैं: इनमें dipole-dipole attraction है par O-H donor नहीं, तो ये समान mass के alcohols से नीचे boil करते हैं।
तीसरा, hydrophobic tail भूलना: एक strong polar head water solubility की guarantee नहीं देता अगर chain लंबी हो, जैसा decanoic acid दिखाता है।
चौथा, aromatic carbonyl ring को ortho या para-directing कहना: electron-withdrawing carbonyl groups deactivating aur meta-directing हैं।
Pro-tip: एक five-second force audit चलाइए, हर molecule को dispersion, dipole, hydrogen-bond या dimer label कीजिए, पहले उसी से order कीजिए, फिर ties को mass aur branching से तोड़िए।

Uses questions के लिए, चार classics पर anchor कीजिए जो examiners को पसंद हैं: preserving के लिए formalin, acetic acid के लिए vinegar, adipic acid के लिए nylon-six-six, aur preservative के रूप में sodium benzoate।
aur किसी भी solubility ranking के लिए, एक बार head hydrogen-bond कर सके यह confirm करके, tail length भी नज़र से देख लीजिए।

board_events.text: Every order in this chapter is one question in disguise: how stable is the reacting species or its conjugate base?

segments.text: This recap gathers the whole chapter's quantitative toolkit onto a single board.
The diagram lines up the four orders you will lean on again and again.

The carbonyl constants: an s p two carbon, bond angle near one hundred twenty degrees, a carbon-oxygen bond about one hundred twenty-three picometres and seven hundred forty-five kilojoules per mole, and a dipole moment near two point three to two point eight debye.
The reactivity order toward nucleophilic addition: trichloroacetaldehyde, then methanal, then ethanal, then propanone.

The acidity order: carboxylic acid stronger than phenol stronger than alcohol; and by p K a, trifluoroacetic at zero point two three, below benzoic at four point one nine, below acetic at four point seven six.
The substituent pull series, in order of increasing acidity: phenyl, iodine, bromine, chlorine, fluorine, cyano, nitro, then trifluoromethyl.
And the boiling-point ladder: hydrocarbon below ether below aldehyde and ketone below alcohol below carboxylic acid.
Notice that every order in this chapter is one question in disguise: how stable is the reacting species, or its conjugate base?
यह recap पूरे chapter का quantitative toolkit एक ही board पर इकट्ठा करता है।
Diagram उन chaar orders को line-up करता है जिन पर आप बार-बार टिकेंगे।

Carbonyl constants: एक s p two carbon, bond angle लगभग one hundred twenty degrees, एक carbon-oxygen bond लगभग one hundred twenty-three picometres aur seven hundred forty-five kilojoules per mole, aur एक dipole moment लगभग two point three to two point eight debye।
Nucleophilic addition की तरफ reactivity order: trichloroacetaldehyde, फिर methanal, फिर ethanal, फिर propanone।

Acidity order: carboxylic acid, phenol से strong, phenol alcohol से strong; aur p K a से, trifluoroacetic zero point two three पर, benzoic four point one nine से नीचे, acetic four point seven six से नीचे।
Substituent pull series, बढ़ती acidity के order में: phenyl, iodine, bromine, chlorine, fluorine, cyano, nitro, फिर trifluoromethyl।
aur boiling-point ladder: hydrocarbon, ether से नीचे, aldehyde aur ketone से नीचे, alcohol से नीचे, carboxylic acid से नीचे।
ध्यान दीजिए कि इस chapter का हर order एक ही सवाल का भेस है: reacting species, या उसकी conjugate base, कितनी stable है?

board_events.text: The whole chapter on one board
Carbonyl $>\!C{=}O$: $sp^2$, trigonal, $C$ electrophilic / $O$ nucleophilic; general formula $C_nH_{2n}O$ (functional isomers).
Naming: $-al$ (CHO is C-1, no locant) / $-one$ (lowest locant) / $-oic$ acid (C-1); suffix priority acid $>$ ester $>$ ... $>$ aldehyde $>$ ketone $>$ alcohol.
Ald/ket prep: oxidise or dehydrogenate alcohols, ozonolysis, alkyne hydration; Rosenmund/Stephen/DIBAL/Étard (ald), dialkylcadmium/Friedel–Crafts (ket).

Ald/ket reactions: Nu addition (HCN, $NaHSO_3$, RMgX, acetal); $H_2N{-}Z$; reduce (NaBH$_4$/LiAlH$_4$; Clemmensen acid / Wolff–Kishner base); Tollens/Fehling = aldehyde only; aldol ($\alpha$-H); Cannizzaro (no $\alpha$-H); iodoform ($CH_3CO$).

Acids: acidity acid $>$ phenol $>$ alcohol; bicarbonate $CO_2$ test; prep by oxidation, hydrolysis, Grignard $+CO_2$; esterification (acyl substitution), $SOCl_2$, amide, LiAlH$_4$/diborane (not NaBH$_4$), decarboxylation, HVZ; ring deactivating, meta.
Physical: b.p. hydrocarbon $<$ ether $<$ ald $\approx$ ket $<$ alcohol $<$ acid (dimer); solubility falls with tail; aromatic carbonyl deactivating, meta-directing.
Uses: formalin/bakelite, acetaldehyde$\to$acetic, acetone/MEK solvents; formic, acetic, adipic (nylon-6,6), sodium benzoate, fatty acids (soap).

segments.text: Here is the entire chapter, distilled onto one board for last-minute revision.
The carbonyl: an s p two, trigonal group, with an electrophilic carbon and a nucleophilic oxygen, and the shared formula C-n-H-two-n-O that makes aldehydes and ketones functional isomers.

Naming: use -al for aldehydes, where the C H O is carbon one with no locant; -one for ketones, at the lowest locant; and -oic acid, carbon one; with suffix priority running acid, ester, and so on, down to aldehyde, ketone, alcohol.

Aldehyde and ketone preparation: oxidise or dehydrogenate alcohols, ozonolyse alkenes, hydrate alkynes; use Rosenmund, Stephen, DIBAL-H or Etard for aldehydes, and dialkylcadmium or Friedel-Crafts for ketones.

Their reactions: nucleophilic addition with hydrogen cyanide, bisulphite, Grignard and acetals; addition-elimination with ammonia derivatives; reduction to alcohol or, with Clemmensen in acid or Wolff-Kishner in base, to a hydrocarbon; Tollens and Fehling for aldehydes only; aldol when there is alpha-H; Cannizzaro when there is none; and iodoform for a methyl carbonyl.

Acids: acidity runs acid above phenol above alcohol; the bicarbonate carbon-dioxide test identifies them; prepare by oxidation, hydrolysis, or Grignard plus carbon dioxide; react by esterification, thionyl chloride, amide formation, reduction with lithium aluminium hydride or diborane but not borohydride, decarboxylation and the H V Z reaction; and on a ring they are deactivating and meta-directing.

Physical properties: boiling point runs hydrocarbon below ether below aldehyde and ketone below alcohol below acid, thanks to the dimer; solubility falls as the tail grows; and aromatic carbonyls are deactivating and meta-directing.
Uses: formalin and bakelite, acetaldehyde to acetic acid, acetone and methyl ethyl ketone as solvents; and formic, acetic, adipic for nylon-six-six, sodium benzoate, and fatty acids for soap.
यह रहा पूरा chapter, last-minute revision के लिए एक board पर distilled।
Carbonyl: एक s p two, trigonal group, जिसमें electrophilic carbon aur nucleophilic oxygen है, aur shared formula C-n-H-two-n-O जो aldehydes aur ketones को functional isomers बनाता है।

Naming: aldehydes के लिए -al, जहाँ C H O carbon one है बिना locant; ketones के लिए -one, lowest locant पर; aur -oic acid, carbon one; suffix priority acid, ester, aur ऐसे ही, नीचे aldehyde, ketone, alcohol तक।

Aldehyde aur ketone preparation: alcohols को oxidise या dehydrogenate कीजिए, alkenes को ozonolyse, alkynes को hydrate; aldehydes के लिए Rosenmund, Stephen, DIBAL-H या Etard, aur ketones के लिए dialkylcadmium या Friedel-Crafts।

इनकी reactions: hydrogen cyanide, bisulphite, Grignard aur acetals के साथ nucleophilic addition; ammonia derivatives के साथ addition-elimination; alcohol तक reduction या, acid में Clemmensen या base में Wolff-Kishner से, hydrocarbon तक; Tollens aur Fehling सिर्फ aldehydes के लिए; alpha-H हो तो aldol; ना हो तो Cannizzaro; aur methyl carbonyl के लिए iodoform।

Acids: acidity acid, phenol से ऊपर, phenol alcohol से ऊपर; bicarbonate carbon-dioxide test इन्हें पहचानता है; oxidation, hydrolysis, या Grignard plus carbon dioxide से prepare कीजिए; esterification, thionyl chloride, amide formation, lithium aluminium hydride या diborane से reduction par borohydride से नहीं, decarboxylation aur H V Z reaction से react कीजिए; aur ring पर ये deactivating aur meta-directing हैं।

Physical properties: boiling point hydrocarbon, ether से नीचे, aldehyde aur ketone से नीचे, alcohol से नीचे, acid से नीचे, dimer की बदौलत; solubility tail बढ़ने पर गिरती है; aur aromatic carbonyls deactivating aur meta-directing हैं।

Uses: formalin aur bakelite, acetaldehyde से acetic acid, acetone aur methyl ethyl ketone solvents के रूप में; aur formic, acetic, adipic nylon-six-six के लिए, sodium benzoate, aur fatty acids soap के लिए।
